{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_75393a098ca44803ae097c4b2d543199",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/artifact-shepherding-staged-rollout-and-rollback-contract-2026.json",
    "title": "Artifact shepherding: staged rollout and rollback contract",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Artifact shepherding: staged rollout and rollback contract\",\n  \"space\": \"eng-private-deployments\",\n  \"author\": \"Maya Chen\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-02-15\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-08-03\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Liam O'Rourke\",\n    \"Priya Singh\",\n    \"Diego Morales\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"upgrade-contract\",\n    \"rollback-playbook\",\n    \"canary\",\n    \"telemetry\",\n    \"artifact-signing\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/forensic-friendly-rollback-protocol-and-telemetry-preservation-2026\",\n    \"/confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/private-deploy-operator-handshake-and-runtime-guardrails-2026\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"restricted\",\n  \"body\": \"Overview\\nThis document defines the artifact shepherding contract for staged rollouts and rollbacks on Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. It formalizes the signals, gating thresholds, operator procedures, and evidence-retention requirements that must be satisfied for a model or runtime artifact to progress through canary -> ramp -> full release, and the exact steps to safely rollback. It applies to control-plane and data-plane artifacts (serving runtime binaries, model bundles, quantized weights, kernel patches, operator images).\\n\\nScope\\n- Applies to all private-deploy customer environments managed by Redwood (VPC and on-prem packaged installs).\\n- Covers: artifact signing & provenance, preflight validation, canary orchestration, automated and manual rollback triggers, post-rollback forensic evidence collection.\\n- Excludes: customer-managed model training pipelines and customer-owned third-party appliances (see related_pages for handoff guidance).\\n\\nGoals\\n- Minimize customer-facing impact during upgrades.\\n- Ensure deterministic rollback that preserves customer state and audit evidence.\\n- Provide clear, reproducible operator playbook for on-call and field engineers.\\n\\nKey roles and ownership\\n- Release Owner (engineering): owns stage gating, artifact bundles, and the rollout schedule.\\n- Field Operator (operator / customer engineering): executes rollout and rollback in the customer environment and performs local verification.\\n- SRE Oncall: monitors platform-level SLOs and authorizes emergency rollback if automated circuits do not trigger.\\n- Security/Compliance Reviewer: verifies artifact provenance (signatures, SBOM) for regulated customers before ramp.\\n\\nPrerequisites (pre-release checklist)\\n1. Artifact packaging: each bundle must include a signed manifest (COSE/PKCS7) and SBOM. The manifest contains: semantic_version, checksums (sha256), compatible_runtime_ids, and rollback_guard_tags.\\n2. Operator tools: field environment must have redwoodctl >= 1.12.0 installed, with operator credentials and a valid operator-session token.\\n3. Telemetry contract: customer telemetry export must include these metrics at 30s resolution: request_per_sec, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tok_per_request, model_error_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate.\\n4. Backup: snapshot of KV cache and stateful operator artifacts taken and stored off-host. Snapshot command: redwoodctl snapshot create --name pre-release-<artifact>-YYYYMMDD.\\n\\nStaged rollout strategy (canonical flow)\\n1) Canary (0 -> 2%):\\n   - Deploy artifact to a small canary cohort (2% traffic or 1 small tenant, whichever is more conservative).\\n   - Retain both old and new model weights and the ability to route by tenant.\\n   - Minimum dwell time: 30 minutes or 10k requests, whichever is reached first.\\n   - Automatic gating checks (see gating criteria) run continuously.\\n2) Ramp (2% -> 25%):\\n   - Increase traffic in timed increments: 2% -> 10% -> 25% over 2 hours, pausing 20 minutes at each step to validate.\\n   - At each pause, run the full validation suite: synthetic traces, baseline eval prompts, and production smoke queries as described in Validation section.\\n3) Broad roll (25% -> 100%):\\n   - Continue to 50% then 100% only after passing two consecutive ramp windows with green signals and signoff from Release Owner.\\n\\nGating criteria (automated triggers)\\n- Abort and immediate rollback if any of the following are observed during a dwell window: \\n  - Absolute error-rate increase: model_error_rate increases by >0.5 percentage points and the delta is statistically significant with p<0.01 over the last 30 minutes.\\n  - Latency degradation: p95_latency_ms increases by >50% or exceeds 500ms sustained for 10 minutes.\\n  - Token budget regressions: tok_per_request increases >25% without commensurate quality improvement (see quality checks).\\n  - KV cache regressions: kv_cache_hit_rate drops by >15% leading to >10% increase in back-end load.\\n  - Resource saturation: GPU utilization >95% on primary nodes for >5 minutes.\\n- Soft warning thresholds: p50 latency increase >20%, error-rate increase >0.2pp \\u2014 these notify SRE and Release Owner and pause automatic ramps pending review.\\n\\nManual rollback criteria (operator discretion)\\n- Single-customer severe error (data corruption, PII exposure), or customer SLA breach.\\n- Failed dependency rollout (e.g., operator CRD changed and was not applied correctly).\\n- Security or compliance compromise detected in SBOM or signature validation.\\n\\nRollback procedures (ordered checklist)\\n1. Initiate rollback command (preferred automated path if gated):\\n   - redwoodctl rollout rollback --target <deployment-id> --to-version <previous-semver> --preserve-snapshots\\n2. If automated rollback fails or is unavailable, perform explicit operator fallback:\\n   - Step A: Quiesce incoming traffic to the affected tenant cohort: redwoodctl traffic set-weights --deployment <id> --weights old:100,new:0\\n   - Step B: Restore model artifact and runtime image from signed archive: redwoodctl image install --from s3://redwood-artifacts/<artifact>-vX.Y.Z --verify-signature\\n   - Step C: Apply operator manifest rollback: kubectl -n redwood operator set image redwood-operator=redwood/operator:<previous-tag>\\n   - Step D: Rehydrate state from snapshot if required: redwoodctl snapshot restore --name pre-release-<artifact>-YYYYMMDD --target <deployment-id>\\n3. Post-rollback verification (must complete before closing incident):\\n   - Verify all gating metrics are within pre-release baseline for 60 minutes.\\n   - Run smoke test suite (listed in Validation).\\n   - Confirm no loss of persistent requests and that KV cache coherence is restored.\\n4. Evidence capture: collect operator logs, artifact manifests, signature verification output, and telemetry windows for the entire rollout and rollback period. Store in the evidence bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/<customer-id>/<artifact>-YYYYMMDD/. Preserve for minimum 90 days for regulated customers.\\n\\nValidation and acceptance tests (examples)\\n- Baseline eval prompts: 200 prompt set used to compare semantic deviation. Pass criteria: mean semantic-similarity drop <0.02 measured with the approved comparator model.\\n- Synthetic throughput run: 30-minute steady-state at 1.5x expected QPS with 95th percentile latency < configured SLO.\\n- End-to-end trace checks: sampled requests must show no >2% increase in external service calls (upstream indices, database) attributable to artifact change.\\n\\nTelemetry and monitoring contract\\n- Required dashboards: \\\"Artifact Rollout Overview\\\", \\\"Canary Health Summary\\\", \\\"KV Cache Drift\\\", and \\\"Model Quality Regression\\\".\\n- Alerting: automated must-fail alerts for gating criteria must notify SRE, Field Operator, and Release Owner via the oncall channel and create a paging incident if severity is P1.\\n- Sampling: preserve full traces for 2 hours, aggregated metrics for 30 days, and raw request logs for 7 days by default. For customers with compliance needs, extend to 365 days as per their telemetry SLA.\\n\\nForensic and audit tasks after rollback\\n- Freeze related telemetry windows for the duration of the investigation.\\n- Generate artifact provenance report: include manifest signatures, uploader identity, and SBOM diff between versions.\\n- If data exposure is suspected, follow the private-deploy evidence-preservation playbook (see related_pages).\\n\\nPost-release remediation and learnings\\n- Required deliverables within 72 hours of rollback: a short incident brief (what changed, why gate failed, immediate fixes), and a remediation plan with owner and ETA.\\n- Release Owner must create a follow-up action ticket for any required runtime or model quantization adjustments.\\n- If rollback was triggered by quality regression, add failing prompts to the guarded prompt set and schedule a regression evaluation in the next model onboarding sprint.\\n\\nAppendix A \\u2014 Example gating table (human-readable)\\nRows: Metric | Baseline | Abort delta | Soft warning\\n- model_error_rate | 0.6% | +0.5pp (abort) | +0.2pp (warn)\\n- p95_latency_ms | 180ms | +50% or >500ms (abort) | +20% (warn)\\n- kv_cache_hit_rate | 72% | -15pp (abort) | -8pp (warn)\\n- gpu_util | 65% | >95% sustained 5m (abort) | 80% (warn)\\n\\nAppendix B \\u2014 Quick CLI cheatsheet\\n- Create snapshot: redwoodctl snapshot create --name pre-release-<artifact>-$(date +%F)\\n- Start canary: redwoodctl rollout start --deployment <id> --artifact <artifact-uri> --stage canary --canary-percent 2\\n- Check rollout status: redwoodctl rollout status --deployment <id>\\n- Force rollback: redwoodctl rollout rollback --deployment <id> --to-version <previous-semver>\\n\\nAppendix C \\u2014 Escalation matrix\\n- 0\\u201315 minutes: Field Operator triages and attempts automated rollback.\\n- 15\\u201360 minutes: SRE oncall engaged; Release Owner notified.\\n- >60 minutes or data-loss event: Executive on-call and Security engaged, customer CS lead notified.\\n\\nReferences and related pages\\n- See related_pages for the forensic rollback protocol and operator handshake runbooks.\\n- SBOM and signature guidelines: /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/artifact-signing-guidelines (internal link).\\n\\nRevision history\\n- 2026-02-15: Initial draft (Maya Chen).\\n- 2026-06-01: Added telemetry contract and gating percentiles (reviewers: Liam O'Rourke).\\n- 2026-08-03: Tightened canary dwell time and added evidence retention for regulated customers (reviewers: Priya Singh, Diego Morales).\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"body\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_75393a098ca44803ae097c4b2d543199\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Artifact shepherding: staged rollout and rollback contract\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/artifact-shepherding-staged-rollout-and-rollback-contract-2026.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: eng-private-deployments\n\n- deploy - operator - handshake - and - runtime - guardrails - 2026 confidentiality : restricted body : overview this document defines the artifact shepherding contract for staged rollouts and rollbacks on redwood private ( vpc / on - prem ) deployments. it formalizes the signals, gating thresholds, operator procedures, and evidence - retention requirements that must be satisfied for a model or runtime artifact to progress through canary - > ramp - > full release, and the exact steps to safely rollback. it applies to control - plane and data - plane artifacts ( serving runtime binaries, model bundles, quantized weights, kernel patches, operator images ).",

document.title: Artifact shepherding: staged rollout and rollback contract
document.content:
{
  "title": "Artifact shepherding: staged rollout and rollback contract",
  "space": "eng-private-deployments",
  "author": "Maya Chen",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-02-15",
  "last_updated": "2026-08-03",
  "reviewers": [
    "Liam O'Rourke",
    "Priya Singh",
    "Diego Morales"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "upgrade-contract",
    "rollback-playbook",
    "canary",
    "telemetry",
    "artifact-signing"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "/confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/forensic-friendly-rollback-protocol-and-telemetry-preservation-2026",
    "/confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/private-deploy-operator-handshake-and-runtime-guardrails-2026"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "restricted",
  "body": "Overview
This document defines the artifact shepherding contract for staged rollouts and rollbacks on Redwood Private (VPC / on-prem) deployments. It formalizes the signals, gating thresholds, operator procedures, and evidence-retention requirements that must be satisfied for a model or runtime artifact to progress through canary -> ramp -> full release, and the exact steps to safely rollback. It applies to control-plane and data-plane artifacts (serving runtime binaries, model bundles, quantized weights, kernel patches, operator images).

Scope
- Applies to all private-deploy customer environments managed by Redwood (VPC and on-prem packaged installs).
- Covers: artifact signing & provenance, preflight validation, canary orchestration, automated and manual rollback triggers, post-rollback forensic evidence collection.
- Excludes: customer-managed model training pipelines and customer-owned third-party appliances (see related_pages for handoff guidance).

Goals
- Minimize customer-facing impact during upgrades.
- Ensure deterministic rollback that preserves customer state and audit evidence.
- Provide clear, reproducible operator playbook for on-call and field engineers.

Key roles and ownership
- Release Owner (engineering): owns stage gating, artifact bundles, and the rollout schedule.
- Field Operator (operator / customer engineering): executes rollout and rollback in the customer environment and performs local verification.
- SRE Oncall: monitors platform-level SLOs and authorizes emergency rollback if automated circuits do not trigger.
- Security/Compliance Reviewer: verifies artifact provenance (signatures, SBOM) for regulated customers before ramp.

Prerequisites (pre-release checklist)
1. Artifact packaging: each bundle must include a signed manifest (COSE/PKCS7) and SBOM. The manifest contains: semantic_version, checksums (sha256), compatible_runtime_ids, and rollback_guard_tags.
2. Operator tools: field environment must have redwoodctl >= 1.12.0 installed, with operator credentials and a valid operator-session token.
3. Telemetry contract: customer telemetry export must include these metrics at 30s resolution: request_per_sec, p50_latency_ms, p95_latency_ms, tok_per_request, model_error_rate, kv_cache_hit_rate.
4. Backup: snapshot of KV cache and stateful operator artifacts taken and stored off-host. Snapshot command: redwoodctl snapshot create --name pre-release-<artifact>-YYYYMMDD.

Staged rollout strategy (canonical flow)
1) Canary (0 -> 2%):
   - Deploy artifact to a small canary cohort (2% traffic or 1 small tenant, whichever is more conservative).
   - Retain both old and new model weights and the ability to route by tenant.
   - Minimum dwell time: 30 minutes or 10k requests, whichever is reached first.
   - Automatic gating checks (see gating criteria) run continuously.
2) Ramp (2% -> 25%):
   - Increase traffic in timed increments: 2% -> 10% -> 25% over 2 hours, pausing 20 minutes at each step to validate.
   - At each pause, run the full validation suite: synthetic traces, baseline eval prompts, and production smoke queries as described in Validation section.
3) Broad roll (25% -> 100%):
   - Continue to 50% then 100% only after passing two consecutive ramp windows with green signals and signoff from Release Owner.

Gating criteria (automated triggers)
- Abort and immediate rollback if any of the following are observed during a dwell window: 
  - Absolute error-rate increase: model_error_rate increases by >0.5 percentage points and the delta is statistically significant with p<0.01 over the last 30 minutes.
  - Latency degradation: p95_latency_ms increases by >50% or exceeds 500ms sustained for 10 minutes.
  - Token budget regressions: tok_per_request increases >25% without commensurate quality improvement (see quality checks).
  - KV cache regressions: kv_cache_hit_rate drops by >15% leading to >10% increase in back-end load.
  - Resource saturation: GPU utilization >95% on primary nodes for >5 minutes.
- Soft warning thresholds: p50 latency increase >20%, error-rate increase >0.2pp — these notify SRE and Release Owner and pause automatic ramps pending review.

Manual rollback criteria (operator discretion)
- Single-customer severe error (data corruption, PII exposure), or customer SLA breach.
- Failed dependency rollout (e.g., operator CRD changed and was not applied correctly).
- Security or compliance compromise detected in SBOM or signature validation.

Rollback procedures (ordered checklist)
1. Initiate rollback command (preferred automated path if gated):
   - redwoodctl rollout rollback --target <deployment-id> --to-version <previous-semver> --preserve-snapshots
2. If automated rollback fails or is unavailable, perform explicit operator fallback:
   - Step A: Quiesce incoming traffic to the affected tenant cohort: redwoodctl traffic set-weights --deployment <id> --weights old:100,new:0
   - Step B: Restore model artifact and runtime image from signed archive: redwoodctl image install --from s3://redwood-artifacts/<artifact>-vX.Y.Z --verify-signature
   - Step C: Apply operator manifest rollback: kubectl -n redwood operator set image redwood-operator=redwood/operator:<previous-tag>
   - Step D: Rehydrate state from snapshot if required: redwoodctl snapshot restore --name pre-release-<artifact>-YYYYMMDD --target <deployment-id>
3. Post-rollback verification (must complete before closing incident):
   - Verify all gating metrics are within pre-release baseline for 60 minutes.
   - Run smoke test suite (listed in Validation).
   - Confirm no loss of persistent requests and that KV cache coherence is restored.
4. Evidence capture: collect operator logs, artifact manifests, signature verification output, and telemetry windows for the entire rollout and rollback period. Store in the evidence bucket: s3://redwood-evidence/<customer-id>/<artifact>-YYYYMMDD/. Preserve for minimum 90 days for regulated customers.

Validation and acceptance tests (examples)
- Baseline eval prompts: 200 prompt set used to compare semantic deviation. Pass criteria: mean semantic-similarity drop <0.02 measured with the approved comparator model.
- Synthetic throughput run: 30-minute steady-state at 1.5x expected QPS with 95th percentile latency < configured SLO.
- End-to-end trace checks: sampled requests must show no >2% increase in external service calls (upstream indices, database) attributable to artifact change.

Telemetry and monitoring contract
- Required dashboards: "Artifact Rollout Overview", "Canary Health Summary", "KV Cache Drift", and "Model Quality Regression".
- Alerting: automated must-fail alerts for gating criteria must notify SRE, Field Operator, and Release Owner via the oncall channel and create a paging incident if severity is P1.
- Sampling: preserve full traces for 2 hours, aggregated metrics for 30 days, and raw request logs for 7 days by default. For customers with compliance needs, extend to 365 days as per their telemetry SLA.

Forensic and audit tasks after rollback
- Freeze related telemetry windows for the duration of the investigation.
- Generate artifact provenance report: include manifest signatures, uploader identity, and SBOM diff between versions.
- If data exposure is suspected, follow the private-deploy evidence-preservation playbook (see related_pages).

Post-release remediation and learnings
- Required deliverables within 72 hours of rollback: a short incident brief (what changed, why gate failed, immediate fixes), and a remediation plan with owner and ETA.
- Release Owner must create a follow-up action ticket for any required runtime or model quantization adjustments.
- If rollback was triggered by quality regression, add failing prompts to the guarded prompt set and schedule a regression evaluation in the next model onboarding sprint.

Appendix A — Example gating table (human-readable)
Rows: Metric | Baseline | Abort delta | Soft warning
- model_error_rate | 0.6% | +0.5pp (abort) | +0.2pp (warn)
- p95_latency_ms | 180ms | +50% or >500ms (abort) | +20% (warn)
- kv_cache_hit_rate | 72% | -15pp (abort) | -8pp (warn)
- gpu_util | 65% | >95% sustained 5m (abort) | 80% (warn)

Appendix B — Quick CLI cheatsheet
- Create snapshot: redwoodctl snapshot create --name pre-release-<artifact>-$(date +%F)
- Start canary: redwoodctl rollout start --deployment <id> --artifact <artifact-uri> --stage canary --canary-percent 2
- Check rollout status: redwoodctl rollout status --deployment <id>
- Force rollback: redwoodctl rollout rollback --deployment <id> --to-version <previous-semver>

Appendix C — Escalation matrix
- 0–15 minutes: Field Operator triages and attempts automated rollback.
- 15–60 minutes: SRE oncall engaged; Release Owner notified.
- >60 minutes or data-loss event: Executive on-call and Security engaged, customer CS lead notified.

References and related pages
- See related_pages for the forensic rollback protocol and operator handshake runbooks.
- SBOM and signature guidelines: /confluence/security-and-compliance/audit-logging/artifact-signing-guidelines (internal link).

Revision history
- 2026-02-15: Initial draft (Maya Chen).
- 2026-06-01: Added telemetry contract and gating percentiles (reviewers: Liam O'Rourke).
- 2026-08-03: Tightened canary dwell time and added evidence retention for regulated customers (reviewers: Priya Singh, Diego Morales).

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_a6e7e19f598943b692d84638aa9a9a6d",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/compliance-anchored-rollback-and-evidence-preservation-playbook-2026.json",
    "title": "Compliance-anchored rollback and evidence preservation playbook",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Compliance-anchored rollback and evidence preservation playbook\",\n  \"space\": \"eng-private-deployments\",\n  \"author\": \"Asha Kapoor\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"security\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-01-15\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-06-10\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Jordan Myers\",\n    \"Lina Chen\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"rollback\",\n    \"compliance\",\n    \"audit\",\n    \"evidence\",\n    \"onprem\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/private-deploy-failure-isolation-rollback-playbook-2026\",\n    \"/confluence/security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/private-deploy-compliance-and-evidence-checklist-2025\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"restricted\",\n  \"body\": \"Overview\\n\\nPurpose:\\nThis playbook defines a compliance-first rollback process for Redwood Private deployments and prescribes steps to preserve, collect, and sign evidentiary artifacts during and after rollback operations. It is intended for field operators, on-call SREs, and the security/compliance owners who must produce an auditable trail following a rollback for regulated customers.\\n\\nScope:\\n- Applies to private deployments (VPC and on-prem) running Redwood runtime services and control plane components.\\n- Covers planned and emergency rollbacks that revert deployed software, model bundles, or configuration changes.\\n- Excludes: customer-managed third-party components outside the deployment boundary unless contractually required.\\n\\nAudience:\\n- Field Operators / Deployment Engineers\\n- SRE and Oncall teams\\n- Security & Compliance reviewers\\n- Customer Success leads for affected customers\\n\\nKey goals:\\n- Ensure rollback actions are reversible and attributable.\\n- Preserve tamper-evident artifacts (logs, manifests, checksums, signatures).\\n- Minimize customer downtime while meeting legal/regulatory evidence obligations.\\n\\nRoles & ownership\\n\\n- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates rollback execution and communications. (Owner: oncall SRE)\\n- Evidence Custodian: responsible for collecting, hashing, signing, and storing artifacts in the evidence store. (Owner: Security)\\n- Deployment Lead: executes the technical rollback steps; creates manifests of actions taken. (Owner: Field Ops / Operator team)\\n- Customer Success Liaison: communicates estimated timelines and evidence delivery to customer contacts. (Owner: Customer Success)\\n\\nPre-rollback requirements checklist (MUST):\\n\\n1) Authorization\\n   - IC confirmed rollback authorization per escalation policy and legal holds.\\n   - Customer notification requirement verified (contract SLA/notice windows).\\n\\n2) Snapshot & Telemetry\\n   - Configure and snapshot the following before any change:\\n     * Control plane manifests (kubectl get all, service, deployment, statefulset YAMLs)\\n     * Runtime KV/cache state pointers (if accessible)\\n     * Model bundle metadata (version hashes, quantization profile id)\\n     * Active routing and traffic-split configs\\n\\n3) Evidence Store availability\\n   - Evidence store (internal secured S3 or EFS) reachable and writable.\\n   - HSM/KMS signing key(s) ready and accessible with audit logging enabled.\\n\\n4) Time synchronization\\n   - NTP sync verified on control plane and nodes (clock skew <= 500ms).\\n\\n5) Stakeholder notification\\n   - Customer Success and Security notified with rollback window and evidence expectations.\\n\\nMinimum artifacts to capture (examples and commands)\\n\\n- Cluster & control plane state:\\n  - kubectl get all --all-namespaces -o yaml > pre-rollback-cluster-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS.yaml\\n  - kubectl get configmap,secret --all-namespaces -o yaml > pre-rollback-configs-...yaml\\n\\n- Deployed binary/model artifacts and metadata:\\n  - List deployed model bundles with checksums: curl -sS http://runtime-api/models | jq . > pre-rollback-models.json\\n  - For each model artifact: sha256sum model-file.bin > model-file.bin.sha256\\n\\n- Logs and traces window:\\n  - Export logs for window [-10min, +0]: elasticsearch/stack dump or journaldctl --since\\n  - Tracing spans export (if tracing backend supports snapshot) for the same window\\n\\n- Traffic & routing configuration:\\n  - Snapshot ingress and service-mesh routes: istioctl proxy-config routes --all-namespaces > routes.txt\\n\\n- Operational actions manifest (operator must create):\\n  - operator-actions-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS.md (freeform list of commands to run)\\n\\nEvidence preservation and signing procedure (step-by-step)\\n\\n1) Collect artifacts into a dedicated evidence bundle directory named with ISO timestamp and incident id:\\n   - Example: evidence/INC-20260610-0001/20260610T153200/\\n\\n2) For each artifact:\\n   - Compute SHA256 checksum and append to a checksums file: sha256sum artifact > artifact.sha256\\n   - Record artifact metadata: filename, source host, service, earliest and latest timestamps captured\\n\\n3) Create a manifest.jsonl (one JSON per line) summarizing artifacts. Manifest fields (flat): artifact_name, checksum_sha256, collected_by, host, captured_start, captured_end, purpose\\n   - NOTE: If your tooling cannot produce JSONL, use newline-delimited key:value pairs in the manifest and include a schema header.\\n\\n4) Sign the manifest with the HSM-backed key and store the signature alongside the manifest:\\n   - Example (HSM-backed PKCS#11): \\n     pkcs11-tool --module /usr/lib/softhsm/libsofthsm2.so -l --sign --input-file manifest.jsonl --output-file manifest.jsonl.sig --key-label \\\"evidence-key\\\"\\n\\n5) Upload artifact bundle to Evidence Store with server-side encryption and object immutability:\\n   - aws s3 cp --acl private --sse aws:kms evidence/INC-... s3://redwood-evidence/<inc-id>/ --metadata incident-id=<inc-id> --storage-class STANDARD_IA\\n\\n6) Record chain-of-custody entry in the internal evidence ledger (app) or a signed ledger file:\\n   - Record fields (flat): incident_id, artifact_path, uploader, upload_timestamp, evidence_store_uri, signature_uri\\n\\nRollback execution patterns (safe categories)\\n\\n- Configuration rollback (safe, fast):\\n  1. Revert the ConfigMap/Ingress/service-mesh route to pre-rollback YAML.\\n  2. Apply in single transaction where possible.\\n  3. Verify control plane health and incremental traffic shift back to expected state.\\n\\n- Model or runtime binary rollback (stateful concerns):\\n  1. Drain traffic using service mesh weight shift (10% increments) to minimize impact.\\n  2. Re-deploy previous model bundle or binary into a shadow pool.\\n  3. Warm caches/kv pointers and validate inference correctness on canary subset.\\n  4. Promote to full traffic when verified.\\n\\n- Full node/image rollback (destructive):\\n  1. Preserve node-level forensic snapshots (disk images, system logs) before wiping.\\n  2. Use immutable artifact promotion: do not modify the original image; deploy an explicit previous image tag.\\n\\nRollback step-by-step (canonical flow)\\n\\n1) IC declares rollback and selects rollback type.\\n2) Run pre-rollback checklist; do NOT execute rollback until Evidence Custodian confirms evidence store readiness.\\n3) Collect and sign pre-rollback artifacts as described above.\\n4) Execute rollback using chosen pattern (config/model/node). Capture operator actions line-by-line into actions manifest.\\n5) During rollback, stream minimal real-time audit entries to evidence ledger: action,start_ts,actor,command_hash\\n6) After rollback completes, collect post-rollback artifacts (same set as pre-rollback) and sign them.\\n7) Compare pre/post checksums and record differences in the manifest (delta report).\\n8) Lock the evidence bundle (apply immutability flag) and notify Security + Customer Success.\\n\\nEvidence retention table (recommended minima)\\n\\n- Artifact Type | Retention (default) | Storage class | Rationale\\n- Cluster manifests | 7 years | Object store / WORM | Regulatory auditing (finance/health sectors)\\n- Signed manifests & signatures | 7 years | WORM / cold storage | Verifiable chain-of-custody\\n- Forensic node images | 1 year (or legal hold) | Encrypted cold | Large size; preserve if requested by legal\\n- Logs & traces (raw) | 90 days | Hot + warm | Operational debugging; long-term archived aggregates retained 7 years\\n- Action manifest & operator notes | 7 years | WORM | Human readable audit evidence\\n\\nStorage and access controls\\n\\n- Access to evidence store must be role-based (only Evidence Custodian, Security leads, and Legal).\\n- All retrieval requests logged with justification and requestor. Retrieval must be authorized by Security.\\n- Evidence uploads must use server-side encryption (customer-managed keys if contract requires).\\n- Apply object immutability (S3 Object Lock) or equivalent retained/locked state immediately after upload.\\n\\nPost-rollback validation and reporting\\n\\n- Validation checklist:\\n  - SLO check: latency and error-rate for the affected routes back within 1.5x baseline within 30 minutes.\\n  - Functional check: Smoke test harness (include example curl assertions) against several endpoints.\\n  - Data consistency: KV/kcache pointer checks for drift in the first 1 hour.\\n\\n- Reporting template (deliver to customer and internal audit):\\n  - Incident id, timeline (ISO), justification, artifacts catalog URI, signature URIs, delta summary, action manifest (redacted as necessary), verification results.\\n\\nExample verification commands (illustrative)\\n\\n- Cluster snapshot:\\n  kubectl get all --all-namespaces -o yaml > pre-rollback-cluster.yaml\\n\\n- Compute checksum and sign (local example):\\n  sha256sum pre-rollback-cluster.yaml > pre-rollback-cluster.yaml.sha256\\n  gpg --armor --output pre-rollback-cluster.yaml.sig --detach-sign --local-user redwood-evidence@example.com pre-rollback-cluster.yaml\\n\\n- Upload to evidence store (AWS S3 example):\\n  aws s3 cp ./evidence/ s3://redwood-evidence/<inc>/ --recursive --sse aws:kms --metadata incident-id=<inc>\\n\\nDanger signals and abort conditions\\n\\n- Ongoing data corruption detected in post-rollback checks (stop promotion and escalate).\\n- Missing or failed upload of any signed manifest to the evidence store (do not proceed; open a Safety Hold).\\n- HSM/KMS key unavailability during signing window (do not proceed without manual Security approval).\\n\\nLegal holds and external requests\\n\\n- If there is a legal hold or regulatory request, Evidence Custodian must snapshot and duplicate the bundle to an isolated WORM store; follow Legal team playbook for preservation and eDiscovery.\\n\\nFAQs\\n\\nQ: What if the evidence store is temporarily unreachable?\\nA: Use an encrypted local buffer with strict ACLs; sign artifacts locally and retry upload. Record buffer location and retention policy in the ledger. Do not delete buffered artifacts until uploaded and verified.\\n\\nQ: Are operator commands stored verbatim?\\nA: Yes. Operator action manifests must include commands executed. Sensitive secrets should be redacted before upload; include redaction reasons in the manifest.\\n\\nQ: Who can request evidence retrieval?\\nA: Security, Legal, and authorized Customer Success leads. Retrievals require a justification and are logged.\\n\\nReferences and related reading\\n\\n- Private deploy compliance and evidence checklist (internal)\\n- Failure isolation & rollback playbook (internal)\\n- Security HSM/KMS standard operating procedures\\n\\nAppendix: checklist quick-reference (copyable)\\n\\n- [ ] IC authorization obtained\\n- [ ] Evidence store reachable and HSM available\\n- [ ] NTP sync validated\\n- [ ] Pre-rollback artifacts collected and checksummed\\n- [ ] Manifest signed and uploaded\\n- [ ] Rollback executed with operator actions logged\\n- [ ] Post-rollback artifacts collected and signed\\n- [ ] Delta report produced and uploaded\\n- [ ] Evidence bundle locked and retrievals authorized\\n\\nContact:\\nSecurity evidence team: security-evidence@redwood.ai\\nField ops oncall: field-ops-oncall@redwood.ai\\n\\nChange log:\\n- 2026-01-15: Initial draft by Asha Kapoor\\n- 2026-06-10: Expanded signing procedures and ledger fields; reviewer comments applied by Jordan Myers and Lina Chen\\n\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"body\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_a6e7e19f598943b692d84638aa9a9a6d\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Compliance-anchored rollback and evidence preservation playbook\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/compliance-anchored-rollback-and-evidence-preservation-playbook-2026.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: eng-private-deployments\n\nevidence / private - deploy - compliance - and - evidence - checklist - 2025 confidentiality : restricted body : overview purpose : this playbook defines a compliance - first rollback process for redwood private deployments and prescribes steps to preserve, collect, and sign evidentiary artifacts during and after rollback operations. it is intended for field operators, on - call sres, and the security / compliance owners who must produce an auditable trail following a rollback for regulated customers.",

document.title: Compliance-anchored rollback and evidence preservation playbook
document.content:
{
  "title": "Compliance-anchored rollback and evidence preservation playbook",
  "space": "eng-private-deployments",
  "author": "Asha Kapoor",
  "owner_team": "security",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-01-15",
  "last_updated": "2026-06-10",
  "reviewers": [
    "Jordan Myers",
    "Lina Chen"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "rollback",
    "compliance",
    "audit",
    "evidence",
    "onprem"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "/confluence/eng-private-deployments/upgrade-and-rollback/private-deploy-failure-isolation-rollback-playbook-2026",
    "/confluence/security-and-compliance/compliance-evidence/private-deploy-compliance-and-evidence-checklist-2025"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "restricted",
  "body": "Overview

Purpose:
This playbook defines a compliance-first rollback process for Redwood Private deployments and prescribes steps to preserve, collect, and sign evidentiary artifacts during and after rollback operations. It is intended for field operators, on-call SREs, and the security/compliance owners who must produce an auditable trail following a rollback for regulated customers.

Scope:
- Applies to private deployments (VPC and on-prem) running Redwood runtime services and control plane components.
- Covers planned and emergency rollbacks that revert deployed software, model bundles, or configuration changes.
- Excludes: customer-managed third-party components outside the deployment boundary unless contractually required.

Audience:
- Field Operators / Deployment Engineers
- SRE and Oncall teams
- Security & Compliance reviewers
- Customer Success leads for affected customers

Key goals:
- Ensure rollback actions are reversible and attributable.
- Preserve tamper-evident artifacts (logs, manifests, checksums, signatures).
- Minimize customer downtime while meeting legal/regulatory evidence obligations.

Roles & ownership

- Incident Commander (IC): coordinates rollback execution and communications. (Owner: oncall SRE)
- Evidence Custodian: responsible for collecting, hashing, signing, and storing artifacts in the evidence store. (Owner: Security)
- Deployment Lead: executes the technical rollback steps; creates manifests of actions taken. (Owner: Field Ops / Operator team)
- Customer Success Liaison: communicates estimated timelines and evidence delivery to customer contacts. (Owner: Customer Success)

Pre-rollback requirements checklist (MUST):

1) Authorization
   - IC confirmed rollback authorization per escalation policy and legal holds.
   - Customer notification requirement verified (contract SLA/notice windows).

2) Snapshot & Telemetry
   - Configure and snapshot the following before any change:
     * Control plane manifests (kubectl get all, service, deployment, statefulset YAMLs)
     * Runtime KV/cache state pointers (if accessible)
     * Model bundle metadata (version hashes, quantization profile id)
     * Active routing and traffic-split configs

3) Evidence Store availability
   - Evidence store (internal secured S3 or EFS) reachable and writable.
   - HSM/KMS signing key(s) ready and accessible with audit logging enabled.

4) Time synchronization
   - NTP sync verified on control plane and nodes (clock skew <= 500ms).

5) Stakeholder notification
   - Customer Success and Security notified with rollback window and evidence expectations.

Minimum artifacts to capture (examples and commands)

- Cluster & control plane state:
  - kubectl get all --all-namespaces -o yaml > pre-rollback-cluster-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS.yaml
  - kubectl get configmap,secret --all-namespaces -o yaml > pre-rollback-configs-...yaml

- Deployed binary/model artifacts and metadata:
  - List deployed model bundles with checksums: curl -sS http://runtime-api/models | jq . > pre-rollback-models.json
  - For each model artifact: sha256sum model-file.bin > model-file.bin.sha256

- Logs and traces window:
  - Export logs for window [-10min, +0]: elasticsearch/stack dump or journaldctl --since
  - Tracing spans export (if tracing backend supports snapshot) for the same window

- Traffic & routing configuration:
  - Snapshot ingress and service-mesh routes: istioctl proxy-config routes --all-namespaces > routes.txt

- Operational actions manifest (operator must create):
  - operator-actions-YYYYMMDDTHHMMSS.md (freeform list of commands to run)

Evidence preservation and signing procedure (step-by-step)

1) Collect artifacts into a dedicated evidence bundle directory named with ISO timestamp and incident id:
   - Example: evidence/INC-20260610-0001/20260610T153200/

2) For each artifact:
   - Compute SHA256 checksum and append to a checksums file: sha256sum artifact > artifact.sha256
   - Record artifact metadata: filename, source host, service, earliest and latest timestamps captured

3) Create a manifest.jsonl (one JSON per line) summarizing artifacts. Manifest fields (flat): artifact_name, checksum_sha256, collected_by, host, captured_start, captured_end, purpose
   - NOTE: If your tooling cannot produce JSONL, use newline-delimited key:value pairs in the manifest and include a schema header.

4) Sign the manifest with the HSM-backed key and store the signature alongside the manifest:
   - Example (HSM-backed PKCS#11): 
     pkcs11-tool --module /usr/lib/softhsm/libsofthsm2.so -l --sign --input-file manifest.jsonl --output-file manifest.jsonl.sig --key-label "evidence-key"

5) Upload artifact bundle to Evidence Store with server-side encryption and object immutability:
   - aws s3 cp --acl private --sse aws:kms evidence/INC-... s3://redwood-evidence/<inc-id>/ --metadata incident-id=<inc-id> --storage-class STANDARD_IA

6) Record chain-of-custody entry in the internal evidence ledger (app) or a signed ledger file:
   - Record fields (flat): incident_id, artifact_path, uploader, upload_timestamp, evidence_store_uri, signature_uri

Rollback execution patterns (safe categories)

- Configuration rollback (safe, fast):
  1. Revert the ConfigMap/Ingress/service-mesh route to pre-rollback YAML.
  2. Apply in single transaction where possible.
  3. Verify control plane health and incremental traffic shift back to expected state.

- Model or runtime binary rollback (stateful concerns):
  1. Drain traffic using service mesh weight shift (10% increments) to minimize impact.
  2. Re-deploy previous model bundle or binary into a shadow pool.
  3. Warm caches/kv pointers and validate inference correctness on canary subset.
  4. Promote to full traffic when verified.

- Full node/image rollback (destructive):
  1. Preserve node-level forensic snapshots (disk images, system logs) before wiping.
  2. Use immutable artifact promotion: do not modify the original image; deploy an explicit previous image tag.

Rollback step-by-step (canonical flow)

1) IC declares rollback and selects rollback type.
2) Run pre-rollback checklist; do NOT execute rollback until Evidence Custodian confirms evidence store readiness.
3) Collect and sign pre-rollback artifacts as described above.
4) Execute rollback using chosen pattern (config/model/node). Capture operator actions line-by-line into actions manifest.
5) During rollback, stream minimal real-time audit entries to evidence ledger: action,start_ts,actor,command_hash
6) After rollback completes, collect post-rollback artifacts (same set as pre-rollback) and sign them.
7) Compare pre/post checksums and record differences in the manifest (delta report).
8) Lock the evidence bundle (apply immutability flag) and notify Security + Customer Success.

Evidence retention table (recommended minima)

- Artifact Type | Retention (default) | Storage class | Rationale
- Cluster manifests | 7 years | Object store / WORM | Regulatory auditing (finance/health sectors)
- Signed manifests & signatures | 7 years | WORM / cold storage | Verifiable chain-of-custody
- Forensic node images | 1 year (or legal hold) | Encrypted cold | Large size; preserve if requested by legal
- Logs & traces (raw) | 90 days | Hot + warm | Operational debugging; long-term archived aggregates retained 7 years
- Action manifest & operator notes | 7 years | WORM | Human readable audit evidence

Storage and access controls

- Access to evidence store must be role-based (only Evidence Custodian, Security leads, and Legal).
- All retrieval requests logged with justification and requestor. Retrieval must be authorized by Security.
- Evidence uploads must use server-side encryption (customer-managed keys if contract requires).
- Apply object immutability (S3 Object Lock) or equivalent retained/locked state immediately after upload.

Post-rollback validation and reporting

- Validation checklist:
  - SLO check: latency and error-rate for the affected routes back within 1.5x baseline within 30 minutes.
  - Functional check: Smoke test harness (include example curl assertions) against several endpoints.
  - Data consistency: KV/kcache pointer checks for drift in the first 1 hour.

- Reporting template (deliver to customer and internal audit):
  - Incident id, timeline (ISO), justification, artifacts catalog URI, signature URIs, delta summary, action manifest (redacted as necessary), verification results.

Example verification commands (illustrative)

- Cluster snapshot:
  kubectl get all --all-namespaces -o yaml > pre-rollback-cluster.yaml

- Compute checksum and sign (local example):
  sha256sum pre-rollback-cluster.yaml > pre-rollback-cluster.yaml.sha256
  gpg --armor --output pre-rollback-cluster.yaml.sig --detach-sign --local-user redwood-evidence@example.com pre-rollback-cluster.yaml

- Upload to evidence store (AWS S3 example):
  aws s3 cp ./evidence/ s3://redwood-evidence/<inc>/ --recursive --sse aws:kms --metadata incident-id=<inc>

Danger signals and abort conditions

- Ongoing data corruption detected in post-rollback checks (stop promotion and escalate).
- Missing or failed upload of any signed manifest to the evidence store (do not proceed; open a Safety Hold).
- HSM/KMS key unavailability during signing window (do not proceed without manual Security approval).

Legal holds and external requests

- If there is a legal hold or regulatory request, Evidence Custodian must snapshot and duplicate the bundle to an isolated WORM store; follow Legal team playbook for preservation and eDiscovery.

FAQs

Q: What if the evidence store is temporarily unreachable?
A: Use an encrypted local buffer with strict ACLs; sign artifacts locally and retry upload. Record buffer location and retention policy in the ledger. Do not delete buffered artifacts until uploaded and verified.

Q: Are operator commands stored verbatim?
A: Yes. Operator action manifests must include commands executed. Sensitive secrets should be redacted before upload; include redaction reasons in the manifest.

Q: Who can request evidence retrieval?
A: Security, Legal, and authorized Customer Success leads. Retrievals require a justification and are logged.

References and related reading

- Private deploy compliance and evidence checklist (internal)
- Failure isolation & rollback playbook (internal)
- Security HSM/KMS standard operating procedures

Appendix: checklist quick-reference (copyable)

- [ ] IC authorization obtained
- [ ] Evidence store reachable and HSM available
- [ ] NTP sync validated
- [ ] Pre-rollback artifacts collected and checksummed
- [ ] Manifest signed and uploaded
- [ ] Rollback executed with operator actions logged
- [ ] Post-rollback artifacts collected and signed
- [ ] Delta report produced and uploaded
- [ ] Evidence bundle locked and retrievals authorized

Contact:
Security evidence team: security-evidence@redwood.ai
Field ops oncall: field-ops-oncall@redwood.ai

Change log:
- 2026-01-15: Initial draft by Asha Kapoor
- 2026-06-10: Expanded signing procedures and ledger fields; reviewer comments applied by Jordan Myers and Lina Chen

    "content": "{\n  \"repo\": \"redwood-private-installer\",\n  \"pr_number\": \"27641\",\n  \"title\": \"Add staged controlplane subnet rollout with DNS-stamp and peering guardrails\",\n  \"author\": \"Marisol Vega\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2025-11-20\",\n  \"updated_at\": \"2025-12-02\",\n  \"merged_at\": \"2025-12-02\",\n  \"state\": \"merged\",\n  \"base_branch\": \"main\",\n  \"head_branch\": \"feature/staged-controlplane-rollout-dns-stamp\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Jonas Meyer\",\n    \"Priya Nair\",\n    \"Derek Huang\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"private-installer\",\n    \"terraform\",\n    \"networking\",\n    \"dns\",\n    \"sre\",\n    \"upgrade-tooling\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_linear\": [\n    \"ENG-4823\",\n    \"INFRA-921\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_jira\": [\n    \"SUP-3142\"\n  ],\n  \"ci_status\": \"pass\",\n  \"files_changed_count\": \"12\",\n  \"additions\": \"842\",\n  \"deletions\": \"210\",\n  \"commits\": [\n    \"a1f3b2c: terraform(controlplane): add dns_stamp resource and stamp tags\",\n    \"b2d4e5f: terraform(modules): introduce staged_rollout_principle and canary labels\",\n    \"c3e5f6a: scripts: add upgrade_safe_rollout.sh with preflight checks and rollback steps\",\n    \"d4f6a7b: helm: wire canary subnet selector to installer chart values\",\n    \"e5a7b8c: docs: rollout playbook and troubleshooting notes\"\n  ],\n  \"files_changed\": [\n    \"terraform/modules/controlplane_subnet/main.tf\",\n    \"terraform/modules/controlplane_subnet/outputs.tf\",\n    \"terraform/modules/controlplane_subnet/variables.tf\",\n    \"terraform/modules/peering/README.md\",\n    \"installer/scripts/upgrade_safe_rollout.sh\",\n    \"installer/terraform/rollout.tf\",\n    \"helm/charts/private-installer/values.yaml\",\n    \"helm/charts/private-installer/templates/subnet-canary.yaml\",\n    \"docs/runbooks/controlplane-rollout.md\",\n    \"tests/integration/test_staged_rollout.py\",\n    \"tests/terraform/test_dns_stamp_plan.tf\",\n    \"README.md\"\n  ],\n  \"description\": \"Motivation: customers running Private control planes across large VPCs asked for a safer, automatable way to expand or migrate controlplane subnets across AZ boundaries while preserving DNS ownership and peering safety. This PR introduces a staged rollout pattern for controlplane subnets that combines: 1) a lightweight DNS-stamp mechanism (a stamped TXT/alias that signals DNS precedence and readiness), 2) canary subnet labels and selectors to limit initial traffic, and 3) explicit peering acceptance guardrails to avoid accidental route churn.\\n\\nWhat this changes (single-line summary): additions to the controlplane subnet Terraform module (dns_stamp resource, staged_rollout boolean, canary_label), a rollout orchestration Terraform file and a helper script (upgrade_safe_rollout.sh) which runs preflight checks, performs incremental subnet handoffs, validates DNS-stamp propagation, and can rollback partial changes. Helm chart values are wired so installer operators can toggle canary selectors per-deployment. Integration tests and docs added.\\n\\nImplementation notes: the dns_stamp concept is intentionally conservative: we create a short-lived Route53 TXT record + optional ALIAS pointing to the new controlplane target that acts as a marker for health probes and for downstream resolvers to prefer the new prefix only after stamp validation. The module exposes stamp_ttl and stamp_health_check variables so operators can tune propagation windows. The staged_rollout flow supports two phases: CANARY (0-10% traffic, limited by subnet selectors and SG scoping) and SWEEP (full migration). Peering guardrails add an explicit accept_with_token step (requires the remote account to approve a token, preventing accidental broad accept).\\n\\nChecklist (manual steps and automation covered):\\n- [x] Terraform module changes (backwards compatible defaults)\\n- [x] Add dns_stamp and stamp validation plan in integration tests\\n- [x] Add rollout orchestration script with idempotent operations and safe rollback\\n- [x] Expose helm toggles for canary selectors and stamp-enabled mode\\n- [x] Document runbook and failure modes + alerts to watch\\n\\nHealth checks and CI: unit terraform plan tests and an integration test that spins a mocked Route53 zone were added. CI was initially flaky for the integration test due to a mock timeout; increased retries and the pipeline now passes (see ci/status).\\n\\nSecurity and backwards compatibility: defaults keep staged_rollout disabled; dns_stamp resources are opt-in. SG changes are scoped and use named security-group fragments so existing policies should remain functional. No secrets are added; peering token is ephemeral and logged only at debug level.\\n\\nRollout guidance (operator):\\n1) Toggle staged_rollout=true in terraform for the target workspace. 2) Run terraform apply which creates canary subnets and dns_stamp in a paused state. 3) Run installer/scripts/upgrade_safe_rollout.sh --canary to perform canary handoff; validate endpoints and DNS-stamp propagation. 4) If canary looks good, run --sweep to complete migration. 5) Use --rollback to revert to previous state; the script performs reversal of peering acceptances and removes stamps.\\n\\nRelated: ENG-4823 (staged rollout design), INFRA-921 (Route53 staging behavior).\\n\\nNotes for reviewers: focus on the rollback idempotency of upgrade_safe_rollout.sh and the peering token acceptance flow in terraform/modules/peering. I included a small test harness in tests/integration/test_staged_rollout.py that simulates stamp propagation delays.\\n\\nMerge outcome: squash-merged to main after addressing review feedback.\\n\",\n  \"review_comments\": [\n    \"Jonas Meyer: Left a couple of nit comments on the script logging and suggested we emit a structured event when a stamp transitions to 'validated' so downstream watchers can subscribe. Also questioned whether TXT vs ALIAS is correct tradeoff in cross-account setups.\",\n    \"Marisol Vega (author): Replied that the text stamp is the lowest risk; ALIAS is optional and gated behind a variable. Added a structured CloudWatch metric emit in the script per Jonas' suggestion.\",\n    \"Priya Nair: Asked for an explicit test around SG scoping when canary and sweep subnets co-exist. Added tests/integration/test_staged_rollout.py to cover this scenario.\",\n    \"Derek Huang: Requested a small doc section on how Route53 resolver caching can delay stamp visibility; I expanded docs/runbooks/controlplane-rollout.md with troubleshooting steps and TTL recommendations.\",\n    \"CI bot: initial integration run failed due to mock Route53 timeout; re-run after increasing retry backoff, all checks passed.\"\n  ],\n  \"merge_method\": \"squash\",\n  \"merge_commit_sha\": \"f8c2e3b9d6a4e7b1c3a29d4f2b6e9a3c4d5f6e7a\",\n  \"release_notes\": \"Introduce opt-in staged controlplane subnet rollout: dns_stamp for gradual DNS handoff, canary subnet selectors, peering accept guard with token, and an upgrade_safe_rollout helper script. Backwards compatible and disabled by default.\",\n  \"breaking_change\": \"false\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"description\",\n    \"review_comments\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_b928a31ac74644d2b70298634002bdff\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Add staged controlplane subnet rollout with DNS-stamp and peering guardrails\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/github\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/github/redwood-private-installer/pr-27641-add-staged-controlplane-subnet-rollout-with-dns-stamp-and-peering-guardrails.json\nConnector: github\nWorkspace: redwood-private-installer\n\ndescription : motivation : customers running private control planes across large vpcs asked for a safer, automatable way to expand or migrate controlplane subnets across az boundaries while preserving dns ownership and peering safety. this pr introduces a staged rollout pattern for controlplane subnets that combines : 1 ) a lightweight dns - stamp mechanism ( a stamped txt / alias that signals dns precedence and readiness ), 2 ) canary subnet labels and selectors to limit initial traffic, and 3 ) explicit peering acceptance guardrails to avoid accidental route churn.",

document.content:
{
  "repo": "redwood-private-installer",
  "pr_number": "27641",
  "title": "Add staged controlplane subnet rollout with DNS-stamp and peering guardrails",
  "author": "Marisol Vega",
  "created_at": "2025-11-20",
  "updated_at": "2025-12-02",
  "merged_at": "2025-12-02",
  "state": "merged",
  "base_branch": "main",
  "head_branch": "feature/staged-controlplane-rollout-dns-stamp",
  "reviewers": [
    "Jonas Meyer",
    "Priya Nair",
    "Derek Huang"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "private-installer",
    "terraform",
    "networking",
    "dns",
    "sre",
    "upgrade-tooling"
  ],
  "linked_linear": [
    "ENG-4823",
    "INFRA-921"
  ],
  "linked_jira": [
    "SUP-3142"
  ],
  "ci_status": "pass",
  "files_changed_count": "12",
  "additions": "842",
  "deletions": "210",
  "commits": [
    "a1f3b2c: terraform(controlplane): add dns_stamp resource and stamp tags",
    "b2d4e5f: terraform(modules): introduce staged_rollout_principle and canary labels",
    "c3e5f6a: scripts: add upgrade_safe_rollout.sh with preflight checks and rollback steps",
    "d4f6a7b: helm: wire canary subnet selector to installer chart values",
    "e5a7b8c: docs: rollout playbook and troubleshooting notes"
  ],
  "files_changed": [
    "terraform/modules/controlplane_subnet/main.tf",
    "terraform/modules/controlplane_subnet/outputs.tf",
    "terraform/modules/controlplane_subnet/variables.tf",
    "terraform/modules/peering/README.md",
    "installer/scripts/upgrade_safe_rollout.sh",
    "installer/terraform/rollout.tf",
    "helm/charts/private-installer/values.yaml",
    "helm/charts/private-installer/templates/subnet-canary.yaml",
    "docs/runbooks/controlplane-rollout.md",
    "tests/integration/test_staged_rollout.py",
    "tests/terraform/test_dns_stamp_plan.tf",
    "README.md"
  ],
  "description": "Motivation: customers running Private control planes across large VPCs asked for a safer, automatable way to expand or migrate controlplane subnets across AZ boundaries while preserving DNS ownership and peering safety. This PR introduces a staged rollout pattern for controlplane subnets that combines: 1) a lightweight DNS-stamp mechanism (a stamped TXT/alias that signals DNS precedence and readiness), 2) canary subnet labels and selectors to limit initial traffic, and 3) explicit peering acceptance guardrails to avoid accidental route churn.\n\nWhat this changes (single-line summary): additions to the controlplane subnet Terraform module (dns_stamp resource, staged_rollout boolean, canary_label), a rollout orchestration Terraform file and a helper script (upgrade_safe_rollout.sh) which runs preflight checks, performs incremental subnet handoffs, validates DNS-stamp propagation, and can rollback partial changes. Helm chart values are wired so installer operators can toggle canary selectors per-deployment. Integration tests and docs added.\n\nImplementation notes: the dns_stamp concept is intentionally conservative: we create a short-lived Route53 TXT record + optional ALIAS pointing to the new controlplane target that acts as a marker for health probes and for downstream resolvers to prefer the new prefix only after stamp validation. The module exposes stamp_ttl and stamp_health_check variables so operators can tune propagation windows. The staged_rollout flow supports two phases: CANARY (0-10% traffic, limited by subnet selectors and SG scoping) and SWEEP (full migration). Peering guardrails add an explicit accept_with_token step (requires the remote account to approve a token, preventing accidental broad accept).\n\nChecklist (manual steps and automation covered):\n- [x] Terraform module changes (backwards compatible defaults)\n- [x] Add dns_stamp and stamp validation plan in integration tests\n- [x] Add rollout orchestration script with idempotent operations and safe rollback\n- [x] Expose helm toggles for canary selectors and stamp-enabled mode\n- [x] Document runbook and failure modes + alerts to watch\n\nHealth checks and CI: unit terraform plan tests and an integration test that spins a mocked Route53 zone were added. CI was initially flaky for the integration test due to a mock timeout; increased retries and the pipeline now passes (see ci/status).\n\nSecurity and backwards compatibility: defaults keep staged_rollout disabled; dns_stamp resources are opt-in. SG changes are scoped and use named security-group fragments so existing policies should remain functional. No secrets are added; peering token is ephemeral and logged only at debug level.\n\nRollout guidance (operator):\n1) Toggle staged_rollout=true in terraform for the target workspace. 2) Run terraform apply which creates canary subnets and dns_stamp in a paused state. 3) Run installer/scripts/upgrade_safe_rollout.sh --canary to perform canary handoff; validate endpoints and DNS-stamp propagation. 4) If canary looks good, run --sweep to complete migration. 5) Use --rollback to revert to previous state; the script performs reversal of peering acceptances and removes stamps.\n\nRelated: ENG-4823 (staged rollout design), INFRA-921 (Route53 staging behavior).\n\nNotes for reviewers: focus on the rollback idempotency of upgrade_safe_rollout.sh and the peering token acceptance flow in terraform/modules/peering. I included a small test harness in tests/integration/test_staged_rollout.py that simulates stamp propagation delays.\n\nMerge outcome: squash-merged to main after addressing review feedback.\n",
  "review_comments": [
    "Jonas Meyer: Left a couple of nit comments on the script logging and suggested we emit a structured event when a stamp transitions to 'validated' so downstream watchers can subscribe. Also questioned whether TXT vs ALIAS is correct tradeoff in cross-account setups.",
    "Marisol Vega (author): Replied that the text stamp is the lowest risk; ALIAS is optional and gated behind a variable. Added a structured CloudWatch metric emit in the script per Jonas' suggestion.",
    "Priya Nair: Asked for an explicit test around SG scoping when canary and sweep subnets co-exist. Added tests/integration/test_staged_rollout.py to cover this scenario.",
    "Derek Huang: Requested a small doc section on how Route53 resolver caching can delay stamp visibility; I expanded docs/runbooks/controlplane-rollout.md with troubleshooting steps and TTL recommendations.",
    "CI bot: initial integration run failed due to mock Route53 timeout; re-run after increasing retry backoff, all checks passed."
  ],
  "merge_method": "squash",
  "merge_commit_sha": "f8c2e3b9d6a4e7b1c3a29d4f2b6e9a3c4d5f6e7a",
  "release_notes": "Introduce opt-in staged controlplane subnet rollout: dns_stamp for gradual DNS handoff, canary subnet selectors, peering accept guard with token, and an upgrade_safe_rollout helper script. Backwards compatible and disabled by default.",
  "breaking_change": "false",
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "description",
    "review_comments"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_b928a31ac74644d2b70298634002bdff"
}

    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/google_drive",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"Incremental Snapshot Retention and Rollback Guidance for Private Deployments\",\n  \"owner\": \"Priya Iyer\",\n  \"drive_area\": \"shared_drives\",\n  \"path\": \"shared_drives/engineering/private-deployments/incremental-snapshot-retention-and-rollback-guidance\",\n  \"doc_type\": \"doc\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2024-11-03\",\n  \"last_modified\": \"2026-03-06\",\n  \"collaborators\": [\n    \"Marcus Lee\",\n    \"Sofia Alvarez\",\n    \"Daniel Cho\"\n  ],\n  \"team\": \"eng-private-deployments\",\n  \"status\": \"in_review\",\n  \"tags\": [\n    \"disaster-recovery\",\n    \"snapshots\",\n    \"terraform\",\n    \"on-prem\",\n    \"backup\",\n    \"retention\",\n    \"playbook\"\n  ],\n  \"linked_artifacts\": [\n    \"CONFLUENCE-DR-PLAN-981\",\n    \"JIRA-PRIV-4321\",\n    \"https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-private-deployments/pull/218\"\n  ],\n  \"body\": \"Purpose and scope:\\\\n\\\\nThis doc is a working draft describing an incremental snapshot retention policy and a stepwise rollback/restore guidance for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem packages). It focuses on:\\\\n- safe incremental backups for disks/object stores,\\\\n- consistent restore points across services (control plane DB, model artifacts, KV caches, infrastructure config),\\\\n- Terraform state and module considerations for restore after failure or as part of upgrade rollback, and\\\\n- verification steps and test plans for DR rehearsals.\\\\n\\\\nAudience:\\\\nPrimary: platform engineers, SRE, and solutions engineers who run customer private deployments. Secondary: product security and support on-call.\\\\n\\\\nHigh-level RTO/RPO targets (proposal):\\\\n- Control plane metadata DB (Postgres): RTO 30m, RPO 15m (via WAL shipping / streaming replication + incremental snapshots)\\\\n- Model artifacts (object store): RTO 2h, RPO 1h (incremental object layer + manifest versioning)\\\\n- Serving runtime (GPU state + cache): RTO best-effort (repopulate caches), RPO N/A (caches reconstructed)\\\\n- Terraform state: RTO 1h, RPO ideally 0 (state stored in a versioned backend - see notes)\\\\n\\\\nSnapshot strategy overview:\\\\n1) Multi-layer snapshots:\\\\n   - Block-level incremental snapshots for instance volumes (EBS/ZFS/CEPH) every 30 minutes for critical nodes (control plane), hourly for compute nodes.\\\\n   - Object-store incremental syncs (rsync/rclone/replication to S3-compatible backend) for model artifacts every 15 minutes for active training/ingest clusters, hourly otherwise.\\\\n   - Logical DB backups: base backup nightly + WAL segments retained for 7 days (configured via retention window) and shipped to cold storage.\\\\n\\\\n2) Consistency windows and application quiesce:\\\\n   - For a point-in-time consistent restore across multiple resources, create a coordinated checkpoint: pause writes to the control plane APIs, flush DB WAL, snapshot volumes, then resume. This is required for production-grade consistency; for best RTO tradeoffs, use asynchronous replication with known divergence bounds.\\\\n\\\\n3) Retention policy (recommended starting point):\\\\n   - Short-term retention: keep all incremental snapshots for the last 72 hours.\\\\n   - Mid-term retention: keep hourly consolidated deltas for 7 days.\\\\n   - Long-term retention: keep daily consolidated full snapshot (or manifest) for 90 days.\\\\n   - Archive: weekly full snapshot stored in cold object store for 1 year for compliance customers.\\\\n\\\\nTerraform-specific notes (modules and state):\\\\n- State backend: always use a versioned, tamper-evident backend (e.g., remote backend with object-versioning + server-side encryption + write-once lifecycle for older state snapshots) for terraform.tfstate. For airgapped/offline installs, we maintain an encrypted state artifact pushed to the customer's S3-compatible archive and to a vendor-side store for recovery.\\\\n- Module design considerations: keep infrastructure bootstrap modules idempotent and small. Do not place long-lived, mutable customer data in a module; reference it via data sources.\\\\n- Recovery path for corrupted state: follow recovery steps in the terraform/README for the private-deploy repo: retrieve last known-good state artifact, run terraform init with the recovered backend, plan to detect drift, then terraform apply in a controlled maintenance window.\\\\n- Important modules to track for DR: module.network (VPC/subnet routing), module.storage (object store configuration), module.db (managed Postgres/primary replicas), module.k8s (cluster config). Add a module-level tag `dr-critical` to resources that must be restored before application traffic resumes.\\\\n\\\\nRollback/restore playbook (tagged, actionable steps)\\\\n- Goal: recover to a chosen snapshot point with minimal manual intervention. The numbered steps assume control-plane operator access and an approved incident ticket.\\\\n\\\\n1) Triage and decision:\\\\n   - Confirm incident scope (single node, region, or full cluster). Attach telemetry: instance health, recent deployment PRs, terraform changes, and storage IO errors.\\\\n   - If data corruption suspected, select a point-in-time earlier than the suspected window. For software regressions, consider rolling forward to a patched build if faster than restore.\\\\n\\\\n2) Prepare recovery environment:\\\\n   - Create an incident branch in terraform (name: incident/YYYYMMDD/owner) to avoid accidental changes to main.\\\\n   - Lock the terraform state backend (if supported) to prevent concurrent writes.\\\\n   - If on-prem airgapped: provision a recovery host with access to the snapshot archive (USB/NAS import or S3-compatible endpoint).\\\\n\\\\n3) Retrieve and validate snapshots:\\\\n   - Fetch the control-plane DB base backup + relevant WAL segments. Validate checksums (we store SHA256 in the snapshot manifest).\\\\n   - For object artifacts: download manifest and a sample of files to validate content and sizes.\\\\n   - Validate terraform state artifact integrity against the artifact manifest (pgp/gpg signature where available).\\\\n\\\\n4) Restore sequence (order matters):\\\\n   - Restore network and storage primitives first (VPC routes, object store buckets, volume attachments). Many resources must exist before databases and control-plane services can mount.\\\\n   - Restore DB base backup and replay WAL to the chosen point. Start DB in single-user recovery mode and run smoke SQL tests.\\\\n   - Restore control-plane application metadata (if separate from DB) and run migration rollbacks (if necessary).\\\\n   - Rehydrate model artifacts to object store and validate manifests. For large artifact sets, use concurrent multipart uploads and validate ETags.\\\\n   - Bring up control-plane services with maintenance mode enabled. Wait for health checks and read-only queries to succeed.\\\\n   - Verify telemetry (API responses, example request paths, canary inference) before enabling write traffic.\\\\n\\\\n5) Terraform state reconciliation:\\\\n   - After infrastructure is present, run terraform plan against recovered state to detect drift. Carefully review plan; for destructive changes, require a second approver.\\\\n   - Apply only the minimal set of changes necessary to restore resource attachments (e.g., volume attachments) unless a full reapply was planned.\\\\n\\\\n6) Post-restore validation and smoke tests:\\\\n   - Run end-to-end canaries: token-level inference on a pinned model, model artifact checksums, session restore, and a synthetic high-load test at reduced concurrency.\\\\n   - Validate billing/usage counters and token accounting sanity for the recovered window.\\\\n\\\\n7) Communication and closeout:\\\\n   - Update incident ticket with timeline, chosen snapshot id(s), and root cause hypothesis.\\\\n   - Schedule a postmortem and DR rehearsal if the restore was > 1 hour or if recovery revealed process gaps.\\\\n\\\\nEdge cases and notes:\\\\n- Partial corruption of model artifacts: support repair by re-fetching artifacts from upstream model registry. Maintain a canonical model manifest in a separate versioned store to allow selective re-download.\\\\n- Long-running WAL gaps: if WAL segments are missing, we may have to restore to the last complete base backup. Document the data loss window explicitly and notify stakeholders.\\\\n- Terraform drift vs config rollback: if the incident is a bad terraform change, prefer a state-driven rollback using the last-good state artifact rather than reapplying the bad config. Keep a copy of the PR that triggered the change in linked_artifacts.\\\\n\\\\nTest plan for DR rehearsals (quarterly recommended):\\\\n- Smoke rehearsal (monthly): restore DB to a test namespace, run the canary suite. Validate RTO < 1 hour for control-plane-only restores.\\\\n- Partial restore (quarterly): restore object-store artifacts for one model and validate serving.\\\\n- Full rehearse (biannual): in a non-production region or isolated customer env, perform full coordinated checkpoint and restore to prove end-to-end recovery. Capture timings for RTO/RPO metrics.\\\\n\\\\nTerraform helper snippets (notes for module maintainers):\\\\n- Store tfstate with object versioning enabled. Tag state snapshots with incident metadata: {\\\"incident_id\\\": \\\"JIRA-PRIV-4321\\\", \\\"snapshot_point\\\": \\\"2026-03-05T03:00Z\\\"}.\\\\n- Add lifecycle rules to important resources to prevent accidental deletion: lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true } behind a feature flag.\\\\n- Export a `dr_snapshot_manifest` from the infra bootstrap to central archive (manifest includes SHA256 checksums, creation timestamp, list of snapshots and terraform state id).\\\\n\\\\nOpen questions / TODOs (working list):\\\\n- Decide default retention SLAs for enterprise vs self-hosted customers (pricing implications).\\\\n- Add automated manifest signing for object snapshots (GPG/PGP) and wire a verification step into our restore automation.\\\\n- Define small-footprint recovery tooling for completely airgapped installs (USB import tooling, encrypted keys rotation).\\\\n- Integrate a restore dry-run in the CI for terraform modules to ensure idempotency on a test backend.\\\\n\\\\nAppendix: quick command references (examples, operator scratchpad)\\\\n- List snapshots (example): psnapctl list --cluster-id $CLUSTER --since 72h\\\\n- Download manifest: rclone copy s3:customer-archive/$CLUSTER/manifests/$SNAPSHOT.json ./\\\\n- Verify checksum: sha256sum -c ./snapshot.manifest.sha256\\\\n- Postgres restore skeleton: pg_basebackup -D /var/lib/postgres/data -R -X fetch -z --verbose --label=\\\\\\\"$SNAP_ID\\\\\\\"\\\\n\\\\nNotes to self / rough TODOs:\\\\n- Convert this draft into a short runbook with 1-page quick start, then a detailed appendix for engineers.\\\\n- Pair with security on key management for archived states.\\\\n- Add a simple terraform module test harness for simulated state recoveries.\\\\n\\\\nEnd of draft.\\\\n\\\\n(Informal notes: lots of shorthand above, need to add specific customer examples and map to on-prem storage vendors like NetApp/CEPH, and to cloud object stores for hybrid installs. Also follow up with Marcus on the WAL retention economics spreadsheet - JIRA-PRIV-4321.)\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"body\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_67fd0fa35c704bcbac0e7aa23fcd6285\"\n}",
