document.title: Incremental Snapshot Retention and Rollback Guidance for Private Deployments
document.content:
{
  "title": "Incremental Snapshot Retention and Rollback Guidance for Private Deployments",
  "owner": "Priya Iyer",
  "drive_area": "shared_drives",
  "path": "shared_drives/engineering/private-deployments/incremental-snapshot-retention-and-rollback-guidance",
  "doc_type": "doc",
  "created_at": "2024-11-03",
  "last_modified": "2026-03-06",
  "collaborators": [
    "Marcus Lee",
    "Sofia Alvarez",
    "Daniel Cho"
  ],
  "team": "eng-private-deployments",
  "status": "in_review",
  "tags": [
    "disaster-recovery",
    "snapshots",
    "terraform",
    "on-prem",
    "backup",
    "retention",
    "playbook"
  ],
  "linked_artifacts": [
    "CONFLUENCE-DR-PLAN-981",
    "JIRA-PRIV-4321",
    "https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-private-deployments/pull/218"
  ],
  "body": "Purpose and scope:\\n\\nThis doc is a working draft describing an incremental snapshot retention policy and a stepwise rollback/restore guidance for Redwood Private deployments (VPC and on-prem packages). It focuses on:\\n- safe incremental backups for disks/object stores,\\n- consistent restore points across services (control plane DB, model artifacts, KV caches, infrastructure config),\\n- Terraform state and module considerations for restore after failure or as part of upgrade rollback, and\\n- verification steps and test plans for DR rehearsals.\\n\\nAudience:\\nPrimary: platform engineers, SRE, and solutions engineers who run customer private deployments. Secondary: product security and support on-call.\\n\\nHigh-level RTO/RPO targets (proposal):\\n- Control plane metadata DB (Postgres): RTO 30m, RPO 15m (via WAL shipping / streaming replication + incremental snapshots)\\n- Model artifacts (object store): RTO 2h, RPO 1h (incremental object layer + manifest versioning)\\n- Serving runtime (GPU state + cache): RTO best-effort (repopulate caches), RPO N/A (caches reconstructed)\\n- Terraform state: RTO 1h, RPO ideally 0 (state stored in a versioned backend - see notes)\\n\\nSnapshot strategy overview:\\n1) Multi-layer snapshots:\\n   - Block-level incremental snapshots for instance volumes (EBS/ZFS/CEPH) every 30 minutes for critical nodes (control plane), hourly for compute nodes.\\n   - Object-store incremental syncs (rsync/rclone/replication to S3-compatible backend) for model artifacts every 15 minutes for active training/ingest clusters, hourly otherwise.\\n   - Logical DB backups: base backup nightly + WAL segments retained for 7 days (configured via retention window) and shipped to cold storage.\\n\\n2) Consistency windows and application quiesce:\\n   - For a point-in-time consistent restore across multiple resources, create a coordinated checkpoint: pause writes to the control plane APIs, flush DB WAL, snapshot volumes, then resume. This is required for production-grade consistency; for best RTO tradeoffs, use asynchronous replication with known divergence bounds.\\n\\n3) Retention policy (recommended starting point):\\n   - Short-term retention: keep all incremental snapshots for the last 72 hours.\\n   - Mid-term retention: keep hourly consolidated deltas for 7 days.\\n   - Long-term retention: keep daily consolidated full snapshot (or manifest) for 90 days.\\n   - Archive: weekly full snapshot stored in cold object store for 1 year for compliance customers.\\n\\nTerraform-specific notes (modules and state):\\n- State backend: always use a versioned, tamper-evident backend (e.g., remote backend with object-versioning + server-side encryption + write-once lifecycle for older state snapshots) for terraform.tfstate. For airgapped/offline installs, we maintain an encrypted state artifact pushed to the customer's S3-compatible archive and to a vendor-side store for recovery.\\n- Module design considerations: keep infrastructure bootstrap modules idempotent and small. Do not place long-lived, mutable customer data in a module; reference it via data sources.\\n- Recovery path for corrupted state: follow recovery steps in the terraform/README for the private-deploy repo: retrieve last known-good state artifact, run terraform init with the recovered backend, plan to detect drift, then terraform apply in a controlled maintenance window.\\n- Important modules to track for DR: module.network (VPC/subnet routing), module.storage (object store configuration), module.db (managed Postgres/primary replicas), module.k8s (cluster config). Add a module-level tag `dr-critical` to resources that must be restored before application traffic resumes.\\n\\nRollback/restore playbook (tagged, actionable steps)\\n- Goal: recover to a chosen snapshot point with minimal manual intervention. The numbered steps assume control-plane operator access and an approved incident ticket.\\n\\n1) Triage and decision:\\n   - Confirm incident scope (single node, region, or full cluster). Attach telemetry: instance health, recent deployment PRs, terraform changes, and storage IO errors.\\n   - If data corruption suspected, select a point-in-time earlier than the suspected window. For software regressions, consider rolling forward to a patched build if faster than restore.\\n\\n2) Prepare recovery environment:\\n   - Create an incident branch in terraform (name: incident/YYYYMMDD/owner) to avoid accidental changes to main.\\n   - Lock the terraform state backend (if supported) to prevent concurrent writes.\\n   - If on-prem airgapped: provision a recovery host with access to the snapshot archive (USB/NAS import or S3-compatible endpoint).\\n\\n3) Retrieve and validate snapshots:\\n   - Fetch the control-plane DB base backup + relevant WAL segments. Validate checksums (we store SHA256 in the snapshot manifest).\\n   - For object artifacts: download manifest and a sample of files to validate content and sizes.\\n   - Validate terraform state artifact integrity against the artifact manifest (pgp/gpg signature where available).\\n\\n4) Restore sequence (order matters):\\n   - Restore network and storage primitives first (VPC routes, object store buckets, volume attachments). Many resources must exist before databases and control-plane services can mount.\\n   - Restore DB base backup and replay WAL to the chosen point. Start DB in single-user recovery mode and run smoke SQL tests.\\n   - Restore control-plane application metadata (if separate from DB) and run migration rollbacks (if necessary).\\n   - Rehydrate model artifacts to object store and validate manifests. For large artifact sets, use concurrent multipart uploads and validate ETags.\\n   - Bring up control-plane services with maintenance mode enabled. Wait for health checks and read-only queries to succeed.\\n   - Verify telemetry (API responses, example request paths, canary inference) before enabling write traffic.\\n\\n5) Terraform state reconciliation:\\n   - After infrastructure is present, run terraform plan against recovered state to detect drift. Carefully review plan; for destructive changes, require a second approver.\\n   - Apply only the minimal set of changes necessary to restore resource attachments (e.g., volume attachments) unless a full reapply was planned.\\n\\n6) Post-restore validation and smoke tests:\\n   - Run end-to-end canaries: token-level inference on a pinned model, model artifact checksums, session restore, and a synthetic high-load test at reduced concurrency.\\n   - Validate billing/usage counters and token accounting sanity for the recovered window.\\n\\n7) Communication and closeout:\\n   - Update incident ticket with timeline, chosen snapshot id(s), and root cause hypothesis.\\n   - Schedule a postmortem and DR rehearsal if the restore was > 1 hour or if recovery revealed process gaps.\\n\\nEdge cases and notes:\\n- Partial corruption of model artifacts: support repair by re-fetching artifacts from upstream model registry. Maintain a canonical model manifest in a separate versioned store to allow selective re-download.\\n- Long-running WAL gaps: if WAL segments are missing, we may have to restore to the last complete base backup. Document the data loss window explicitly and notify stakeholders.\\n- Terraform drift vs config rollback: if the incident is a bad terraform change, prefer a state-driven rollback using the last-good state artifact rather than reapplying the bad config. Keep a copy of the PR that triggered the change in linked_artifacts.\\n\\nTest plan for DR rehearsals (quarterly recommended):\\n- Smoke rehearsal (monthly): restore DB to a test namespace, run the canary suite. Validate RTO < 1 hour for control-plane-only restores.\\n- Partial restore (quarterly): restore object-store artifacts for one model and validate serving.\\n- Full rehearse (biannual): in a non-production region or isolated customer env, perform full coordinated checkpoint and restore to prove end-to-end recovery. Capture timings for RTO/RPO metrics.\\n\\nTerraform helper snippets (notes for module maintainers):\\n- Store tfstate with object versioning enabled. Tag state snapshots with incident metadata: {\"incident_id\": \"JIRA-PRIV-4321\", \"snapshot_point\": \"2026-03-05T03:00Z\"}.\\n- Add lifecycle rules to important resources to prevent accidental deletion: lifecycle { prevent_destroy = true } behind a feature flag.\\n- Export a `dr_snapshot_manifest` from the infra bootstrap to central archive (manifest includes SHA256 checksums, creation timestamp, list of snapshots and terraform state id).\\n\\nOpen questions / TODOs (working list):\\n- Decide default retention SLAs for enterprise vs self-hosted customers (pricing implications).\\n- Add automated manifest signing for object snapshots (GPG/PGP) and wire a verification step into our restore automation.\\n- Define small-footprint recovery tooling for completely airgapped installs (USB import tooling, encrypted keys rotation).\\n- Integrate a restore dry-run in the CI for terraform modules to ensure idempotency on a test backend.\\n\\nAppendix: quick command references (examples, operator scratchpad)\\n- List snapshots (example): psnapctl list --cluster-id $CLUSTER --since 72h\\n- Download manifest: rclone copy s3:customer-archive/$CLUSTER/manifests/$SNAPSHOT.json ./\\n- Verify checksum: sha256sum -c ./snapshot.manifest.sha256\\n- Postgres restore skeleton: pg_basebackup -D /var/lib/postgres/data -R -X fetch -z --verbose --label=\\\"$SNAP_ID\\\"\\n\\nNotes to self / rough TODOs:\\n- Convert this draft into a short runbook with 1-page quick start, then a detailed appendix for engineers.\\n- Pair with security on key management for archived states.\\n- Add a simple terraform module test harness for simulated state recoveries.\\n\\nEnd of draft.\\n\\n(Informal notes: lots of shorthand above, need to add specific customer examples and map to on-prem storage vendors like NetApp/CEPH, and to cloud object stores for hybrid installs. Also follow up with Marcus on the WAL retention economics spreadsheet - JIRA-PRIV-4321.)",
  "title_field_name": "title",
  "content_field_names": [
    "body"
  ],
  "dataset_doc_uuid": "dsid_67fd0fa35c704bcbac0e7aa23fcd6285"
}

{
  "document": {
    "id": "dsid_499ce734c806422e980396966f03515b",
    "path": "/knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/vpc-operator-evacuation-and-cutover-checklist-2026.json",
    "title": "VPC operator evacuation and cutover checklist",
    "source": "EnterpriseRAG/confluence",
    "content": "{\n  \"title\": \"VPC operator evacuation and cutover checklist\",\n  \"space\": \"eng-private-deployments\",\n  \"author\": \"Marisol Chen\",\n  \"owner_team\": \"engineering\",\n  \"status\": \"published\",\n  \"created_at\": \"2026-03-02\",\n  \"last_updated\": \"2026-07-15\",\n  \"reviewers\": [\n    \"Samir Patel\",\n    \"Tanya Li\",\n    \"Luis Romero\"\n  ],\n  \"labels\": [\n    \"vpc\",\n    \"evacuation\",\n    \"cutover\",\n    \"operator-runbook\",\n    \"rollback\",\n    \"day-2\"\n  ],\n  \"related_pages\": [\n    \"/confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/tenant-eviction-and-safe-state-sanitization-playbook-2026\",\n    \"/confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/vpc-crossconnect-operational-escape-hatch-playbook-2026\"\n  ],\n  \"confidentiality\": \"internal\",\n  \"body\": \"Purpose\\nThis document is an operator-focused checklist and procedural guide for evacuating VPC tenants and performing controlled cutovers during regional network failures, severe interconnect degradation, or cloud provider maintenance windows. It complements the existing safe-failover playbooks and provides concrete commands, verification steps, and escalation paths for on-call and field operators.\\n\\nScope\\n- Applies to Redwood Private VPC deployments (customer-managed networks and Redwood-managed control plane) where tenant compute or data plane needs planned or emergent redirection.\\n- Covers three evacuation modes: graceful drain, accelerated swap, and emergency quarantine.\\n- Excludes airgap/airgapped on-prem appliance procedures (see onprem-packaging runbooks).\\n\\nSummary of evacuation modes\\n1) Graceful drain: Move traffic off a zone/region with >60 minutes lead time. Preserve KV cache checkpoints, warm workers, and allow in-flight requests to complete. Best for planned maint windows.\\n2) Accelerated swap: Short lead (<60 min) redirect using regional routing policies and cached model fallbacks. Prioritizes availability over cost.\\n3) Emergency quarantine: Immediate isolation of suspected tenant compromise or catastrophic network partition. Operator must snapshot telemetry and preserve evidence before state mutation.\\n\\nOwnership and roles\\n- Primary operator: field operator on duty (first responder for execution).\\n- Oncall SRE: validates telemetry and approves regional policy flips.\\n- Solutions owner (customer success): notified for customer-facing communication.\\n- Incident commander: owns communication cadence and cross-team escalations.\\n\\nPre-evacuation checklist (must complete before any action)\\n- Confirm active incident or scheduled maintenance in status dashboard and Slack #ops.\\n- Validate recent model binary and quantization compatibility: run quick artifact compatibility check (see artifact-check command below).\\n- Ensure at least one healthy fallback region with compatible models and sufficient reserved capacity. Target: 120% of projected peak for next 2 hours.\\n- Snapshot KV cache checkpoint: run redwoodctl kv checkpoint --tenant <TENANT_ID> --preserve-metadata.\\n- Lock rollout gates: set rollout_lock=true in the tenant policy to prevent model swaps during eviction.\\n\\nQuick artifact compatibility check (example)\\n- Command: \\n  redwoodctl artifact verify --tenant $TENANT --model $MODEL_ID --quant $PROFILE\\n- Expected output: \\n  {\\n    \\\"status\\\": \\\"ok\\\",\\n    \\\"backward_compatible\\\": true,\\n    \\\"missing_kernels\\\": []\\n  }\\n\\nEvacuation procedures\\nA. Graceful drain (planned maintenance)\\n1. Notify stakeholders (customer success, security, infra) and create temporary status page entry.\\n2. Scale target fallback region up by +25% capacity: redwoodctl scale --region $FALLBACK --pool reserved --pct 125\\n3. Start KV checkpoint and confirm TTLs: redwoodctl kv checkpoint --tenant $T --wait 300\\n4. Initiate routing slow drain (traffic shift 5% every 2 minutes) via routing policy:\\n   curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing/policies/shift -H \\\"Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN\\\" -d '{\\\"tenant\\\":\\\"'$T'\\\",\\\"from\\\":\\\"us-east-1\\\",\\\"to\\\":\\\"us-west-2\\\",\\\"step_pct\\\":5,\\\"step_interval_s\\\":120}'\\n5. Monitor tail latency and 95th percentile token latency; abort if 95p latency exceeds 2x baseline for >3 windows.\\n6. When traffic <5% on source, cordon nodes and drain workloads with graceful timeout 300s: kubectl cordon $NODE && kubectl drain $NODE --timeout=300s --ignore-daemonsets\\n7. After drain, snapshot runtime logs and mark change in incident timeline.\\n\\nB. Accelerated swap (short lead)\\n1. Validate fallback capacity and model compatibility (quick artifact check).\\n2. Enable accelerated routing policy: set step_pct=25 and step_interval_s=60.\\n3. Pre-warm model caches in fallback region using synthetic prefixes and representative prompt sets: redwoodctl warm --tenant $T --model $MODEL --qps 50 --duration 120\\n4. Execute swap and run verification job (see Verification section). If verification fails, automatic rollback policy will revert after 5 minutes unless operator manually extends.\\n\\nC. Emergency quarantine (compromise or total partition)\\n1. Immediately snapshot telemetry and operator evidence: redwoodctl telemetry export --tenant $T --since \\\"1h\\\" --output /tmp/$T-evidence.tar.gz\\n2. Apply network-policy deny-all for tenant: kubectl apply -f - <<EOF\\napiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1\\nkind: NetworkPolicy\\nmetadata:\\n  name: tenant-quarantine\\n  namespace: tenant-$T\\nspec:\\n  podSelector: {}\\n  policyTypes:\\n  - Egress\\n  - Ingress\\n  ingress: []\\n  egress: []\\nEOF\\n3. Mark incident as security-sensitive and contact security@redwood.com and legal if customer data exposure risk > medium.\\n4. Run forensic snapshot of model artifacts and control-plane audit logs. Do NOT mutate model artifacts until forensic review completes.\\n\\nVerification and acceptance tests\\n- Post-cutover verification (automated):\\n  - healthcheck: /internal/health returns 200 for all endpoints\\n  - sample inference suite (10 representative prompts) latency < baseline * 1.5 and correctness pass rate >= 98% (per tenant eval set)\\n  - KV checkpoint integrity: key-count delta <= 0.5%\\n- Manual checks: survey the QPS distribution, watch for queue buildup, confirm that rate-limiters are functioning.\\n\\nMonitoring thresholds and SLOs\\n- Availability SLO for cutover window: 99.5% (target) measured as successful inference responses / total requests in the 30-minute window post-cutover.\\n- Target alert thresholds:\\n  - 95p token latency > 2x baseline for 3 consecutive 1m windows -> P1 alert to oncall and SRE.\\n  - Error rate increase > 0.5% absolute over baseline for 5 minutes -> P1.\\n  - KV cache miss rate > 10% for 10 minutes -> P2 (operator investigation).\\n\\nRollback policy and criteria\\n- Automatic rollback triggers (system will revert if any condition persists >5 minutes):\\n  - 95p token latency > 3x baseline, or\\n  - Error rate increase > 1.5% absolute, or\\n  - Model compatibility failure reported by artifact verifier.\\n- Manual rollback steps:\\n  1. Pause routing policy (set step_pct=0).\\n  2. Revert traffic to source region using controlplane API: curl -X POST /routing/policies/revert ...\\n  3. Restore KV checkpoint (if necessary): redwoodctl kv restore --tenant $T --checkpoint /snapshots/$T-<ts>.tar.gz --force\\n  4. Re-open nodes for traffic after validation.\\n\\nPost-evacuation tasks and evidence\\n- Create incident timeline with timestamps for each major action and attach KV checkpoint IDs and telemetry bundles.\\n- Run a targeted postmortem if any P1/P0 conditions were observed.\\n- Add lessoned learned to the tenant-runbook and mark the tenant policy with updated evacuation window if needed.\\n\\nConfiguration matrix (reference)\\n|| Item || Recommended value || Notes ||\\n|| Fallback over-provisioning || 120\\u2013150% || Depends on historical burst patterns ||\\n|| KV checkpoint frequency || Every 30 minutes during window || Decrease frequency during high-cost windows ||\\n|| Model warm qps || 20\\u2013100 || Use representative prompt set; avoid training-like workloads ||\\n|| Rollout safety gates || 95p latency, error-rate, kv-integrity || All must be green to proceed beyond 50% traffic shift ||\\n\\nCommon operator troubleshooting commands\\n- Check routing policy status: curl -s https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing/policies/$POLICY | jq\\n- Inspect node drain status: kubectl get pods -n tenant-$T -o wide --field-selector status.phase!=Running\\n- Tail inference logs for tenant: kubectl logs -n tenant-$T -l app=inference -f --since=10m\\n- Reapply kv checkpoint: redwoodctl kv restore --tenant $T --checkpoint $CP_ID\\n\\nCommunication templates (quick)\\n- Customer-facing (short): \\n  Subject: Planned maintenance affecting inference latency for <TENANT>\\n  Body: We will be performing a controlled traffic cutover from region A to region B at <TIME>. We expect a brief period of elevated latency for up to 30 minutes; expected availability is >99.5%. We will notify you when the operation completes.\\n\\n- Internal escalation (Slack):\\n  @oncall-sre P1: initiating accelerated swap for <TENANT>. Fallback region: $REGION. Monitoring: #telemetry. Rolling back if 95p latency > 3x baseline for >5m.\\n\\nRunbook maintenance and links\\n- Owner: Marisol Chen (eng-private-deployments)\\n- Review cadence: quarterly or after any P1/P0 evacuation.\\n- Related: tenant eviction playbook, control plane routing API reference, artifact compatibility guide.\\n\\nAppendix: sample accelerated routing JSON payload\\n{\\n  \\\"tenant\\\": \\\"tenant-12345\\\",\\n  \\\"from\\\": \\\"eu-west-1\\\",\\n  \\\"to\\\": \\\"eu-central-1\\\",\\n  \\\"mode\\\": \\\"accelerated\\\",\\n  \\\"step_pct\\\": 25,\\n  \\\"step_interval_s\\\": 60,\\n  \\\"safety_gates\\\": {\\\"95p_latency_multiplier\\\": 2.0, \\\"error_rate_delta\\\": 0.005, \\\"kv_integrity_delta\\\": 0.01},\\n  \\\"auto_rollback_minutes\\\": 5\\n}\\n\\nIf you find gaps or run into edge cases not covered here, please open an RFC in the eng-private-deployments space and tag the owner.\",\n  \"title_field_name\": \"title\",\n  \"content_field_names\": [\n    \"body\"\n  ],\n  \"dataset_doc_uuid\": \"dsid_499ce734c806422e980396966f03515b\"\n}",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: VPC operator evacuation and cutover checklist\nSource: EnterpriseRAG/confluence\nPath: /knowledge/company/sources/confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/vpc-operator-evacuation-and-cutover-checklist-2026.json\nConnector: confluence\nWorkspace: eng-private-deployments\n\n##gap / airgapped on - prem appliance procedures ( see onprem - packaging runbooks ). summary of evacuation modes 1 ) graceful drain : move traffic off a zone / region with > 60 minutes lead time. preserve kv cache checkpoints, warm workers, and allow in - flight requests to complete. best for planned maint windows. 2 ) accelerated swap : short lead ( < 60 min ) redirect using regional routing policies and cached model fallbacks. prioritizes availability over cost. 3 ) emergency quarantine : immediate isolation of suspected tenant compromise or catastrophic network partition. operator must snapshot telemetry and preserve evidence before state mutation.",

{
  "title": "VPC operator evacuation and cutover checklist",
  "space": "eng-private-deployments",
  "author": "Marisol Chen",
  "owner_team": "engineering",
  "status": "published",
  "created_at": "2026-03-02",
  "last_updated": "2026-07-15",
  "reviewers": [
    "Samir Patel",
    "Tanya Li",
    "Luis Romero"
  ],
  "labels": [
    "vpc",
    "evacuation",
    "cutover",
    "operator-runbook",
    "rollback",
    "day-2"
  ],
  "related_pages": [
    "/confluence/eng-private-deployments/day-2-ops/tenant-eviction-and-safe-state-sanitization-playbook-2026",
    "/confluence/eng-private-deployments/deployment-guides/vpc-crossconnect-operational-escape-hatch-playbook-2026"
  ],
  "confidentiality": "internal",
  "body": "Purpose
This document is an operator-focused checklist and procedural guide for evacuating VPC tenants and performing controlled cutovers during regional network failures, severe interconnect degradation, or cloud provider maintenance windows. It complements the existing safe-failover playbooks and provides concrete commands, verification steps, and escalation paths for on-call and field operators.

Scope
- Applies to Redwood Private VPC deployments (customer-managed networks and Redwood-managed control plane) where tenant compute or data plane needs planned or emergent redirection.
- Covers three evacuation modes: graceful drain, accelerated swap, and emergency quarantine.
- Excludes airgap/airgapped on-prem appliance procedures (see onprem-packaging runbooks).

Summary of evacuation modes
1) Graceful drain: Move traffic off a zone/region with >60 minutes lead time. Preserve KV cache checkpoints, warm workers, and allow in-flight requests to complete. Best for planned maint windows.
2) Accelerated swap: Short lead (<60 min) redirect using regional routing policies and cached model fallbacks. Prioritizes availability over cost.
3) Emergency quarantine: Immediate isolation of suspected tenant compromise or catastrophic network partition. Operator must snapshot telemetry and preserve evidence before state mutation.

Ownership and roles
- Primary operator: field operator on duty (first responder for execution).
- Oncall SRE: validates telemetry and approves regional policy flips.
- Solutions owner (customer success): notified for customer-facing communication.
- Incident commander: owns communication cadence and cross-team escalations.

Pre-evacuation checklist (must complete before any action)
- Confirm active incident or scheduled maintenance in status dashboard and Slack #ops.
- Validate recent model binary and quantization compatibility: run quick artifact compatibility check (see artifact-check command below).
- Ensure at least one healthy fallback region with compatible models and sufficient reserved capacity. Target: 120% of projected peak for next 2 hours.
- Snapshot KV cache checkpoint: run redwoodctl kv checkpoint --tenant <TENANT_ID> --preserve-metadata.
- Lock rollout gates: set rollout_lock=true in the tenant policy to prevent model swaps during eviction.

Quick artifact compatibility check (example)
- Command: 
  redwoodctl artifact verify --tenant $TENANT --model $MODEL_ID --quant $PROFILE
- Expected output: 
  {
    "status": "ok",
    "backward_compatible": true,
    "missing_kernels": []
  }

Evacuation procedures
A. Graceful drain (planned maintenance)
1. Notify stakeholders (customer success, security, infra) and create temporary status page entry.
2. Scale target fallback region up by +25% capacity: redwoodctl scale --region $FALLBACK --pool reserved --pct 125
3. Start KV checkpoint and confirm TTLs: redwoodctl kv checkpoint --tenant $T --wait 300
4. Initiate routing slow drain (traffic shift 5% every 2 minutes) via routing policy:
   curl -X POST https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing/policies/shift -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d '{"tenant":"'$T'","from":"us-east-1","to":"us-west-2","step_pct":5,"step_interval_s":120}'
5. Monitor tail latency and 95th percentile token latency; abort if 95p latency exceeds 2x baseline for >3 windows.
6. When traffic <5% on source, cordon nodes and drain workloads with graceful timeout 300s: kubectl cordon $NODE && kubectl drain $NODE --timeout=300s --ignore-daemonsets
7. After drain, snapshot runtime logs and mark change in incident timeline.

B. Accelerated swap (short lead)
1. Validate fallback capacity and model compatibility (quick artifact check).
2. Enable accelerated routing policy: set step_pct=25 and step_interval_s=60.
3. Pre-warm model caches in fallback region using synthetic prefixes and representative prompt sets: redwoodctl warm --tenant $T --model $MODEL --qps 50 --duration 120
4. Execute swap and run verification job (see Verification section). If verification fails, automatic rollback policy will revert after 5 minutes unless operator manually extends.

C. Emergency quarantine (compromise or total partition)
1. Immediately snapshot telemetry and operator evidence: redwoodctl telemetry export --tenant $T --since "1h" --output /tmp/$T-evidence.tar.gz
2. Apply network-policy deny-all for tenant: kubectl apply -f - <<EOF
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: tenant-quarantine
  namespace: tenant-$T
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  - Ingress
  ingress: []
  egress: []
EOF
3. Mark incident as security-sensitive and contact security@redwood.com and legal if customer data exposure risk > medium.
4. Run forensic snapshot of model artifacts and control-plane audit logs. Do NOT mutate model artifacts until forensic review completes.

Verification and acceptance tests
- Post-cutover verification (automated):
  - healthcheck: /internal/health returns 200 for all endpoints
  - sample inference suite (10 representative prompts) latency < baseline * 1.5 and correctness pass rate >= 98% (per tenant eval set)
  - KV checkpoint integrity: key-count delta <= 0.5%
- Manual checks: survey the QPS distribution, watch for queue buildup, confirm that rate-limiters are functioning.

Monitoring thresholds and SLOs
- Availability SLO for cutover window: 99.5% (target) measured as successful inference responses / total requests in the 30-minute window post-cutover.
- Target alert thresholds:
  - 95p token latency > 2x baseline for 3 consecutive 1m windows -> P1 alert to oncall and SRE.
  - Error rate increase > 0.5% absolute over baseline for 5 minutes -> P1.
  - KV cache miss rate > 10% for 10 minutes -> P2 (operator investigation).

Rollback policy and criteria
- Automatic rollback triggers (system will revert if any condition persists >5 minutes):
  - 95p token latency > 3x baseline, or
  - Error rate increase > 1.5% absolute, or
  - Model compatibility failure reported by artifact verifier.
- Manual rollback steps:
  1. Pause routing policy (set step_pct=0).
  2. Revert traffic to source region using controlplane API: curl -X POST /routing/policies/revert ...
  3. Restore KV checkpoint (if necessary): redwoodctl kv restore --tenant $T --checkpoint /snapshots/$T-<ts>.tar.gz --force
  4. Re-open nodes for traffic after validation.

Post-evacuation tasks and evidence
- Create incident timeline with timestamps for each major action and attach KV checkpoint IDs and telemetry bundles.
- Run a targeted postmortem if any P1/P0 conditions were observed.
- Add lessoned learned to the tenant-runbook and mark the tenant policy with updated evacuation window if needed.

Configuration matrix (reference)
|| Item || Recommended value || Notes ||
|| Fallback over-provisioning || 120–150% || Depends on historical burst patterns ||
|| KV checkpoint frequency || Every 30 minutes during window || Decrease frequency during high-cost windows ||
|| Model warm qps || 20–100 || Use representative prompt set; avoid training-like workloads ||
|| Rollout safety gates || 95p latency, error-rate, kv-integrity || All must be green to proceed beyond 50% traffic shift ||

Common operator troubleshooting commands
- Check routing policy status: curl -s https://controlplane.internal/api/v1/routing/policies/$POLICY | jq
- Inspect node drain status: kubectl get pods -n tenant-$T -o wide --field-selector status.phase!=Running
- Tail inference logs for tenant: kubectl logs -n tenant-$T -l app=inference -f --since=10m
- Reapply kv checkpoint: redwoodctl kv restore --tenant $T --checkpoint $CP_ID

Communication templates (quick)
- Customer-facing (short): 
  Subject: Planned maintenance affecting inference latency for <TENANT>
  Body: We will be performing a controlled traffic cutover from region A to region B at <TIME>. We expect a brief period of elevated latency for up to 30 minutes; expected availability is >99.5%. We will notify you when the operation completes.

- Internal escalation (Slack):
  @oncall-sre P1: initiating accelerated swap for <TENANT>. Fallback region: $REGION. Monitoring: #telemetry. Rolling back if 95p latency > 3x baseline for >5m.

Runbook maintenance and links
- Owner: Marisol Chen (eng-private-deployments)
- Review cadence: quarterly or after any P1/P0 evacuation.
- Related: tenant eviction playbook, control plane routing API reference, artifact compatibility guide.

Appendix: sample accelerated routing JSON payload
{
  "tenant": "tenant-12345",
  "from": "eu-west-1",
  "to": "eu-central-1",
  "mode": "accelerated",
  "step_pct": 25,
  "step_interval_s": 60,
  "safety_gates": {"95p_latency_multiplier": 2.0, "error_rate_delta": 0.005, "kv_integrity_delta": 0.01},
  "auto_rollback_minutes": 5
}

If you find gaps or run into edge cases not covered here, please open an RFC in the eng-private-deployments space and tag the owner.",

item.text: The evidence converges on a clear tension: the fast path minimizes time-to-recovery, but the published staged-rollout contract also requires pre-mutation evidence, snapshot safety, deterministic gates, role approvals, and post-rollback verification. I’m now encoding those as two separate, non-hybrid candidates at the same canonical path.

arguments.title: Private Deployment Rollback — Fast Recovery Policy
arguments.content:
# Private Deployment Rollback — Fast Recovery Policy

Owner: SRE On-call  
Status: candidate  
Scope: Redwood-managed private VPC and on-prem deployments.

## Contract

This policy optimizes for the shortest service-restoration time. When a release causes customer-visible errors, latency regression, artifact incompatibility, security concern, or suspected corruption, the field operator may immediately return all affected traffic to the last-known-good version.

1. Announce rollback in the incident channel and name the affected deployment, current version, previous signed version, and operator.
2. Route the affected cohort to the old version: `redwoodctl traffic set-weights --deployment <id> --weights old:100,new:0`.
3. Run `redwoodctl rollout rollback --target <id> --to-version <previous-semver> --preserve-snapshots`.
4. If automation fails, install the previous signed artifact, revert the operator image, and restore the latest available pre-release snapshot only when state compatibility requires it.
5. Page SRE if restoration is not complete within 15 minutes; engage Security for suspected exposure or provenance failure.
6. Validate smoke tests and the primary latency/error dashboards for 15 minutes, then restore normal incident cadence.
7. After service recovery, attach operator logs, artifact manifest/signature output, snapshot identifier, and the rollback timeline. Produce an incident brief within 72 hours.

## Authority

The field operator may execute immediately. SRE approval is not a prerequisite during active impact. Customer notification and compliance review may follow restoration unless the customer contract explicitly blocks the action.

## Abort triggers

Rollback on any severe customer-visible regression, model compatibility failure, or operator judgment that continued rollout increases blast radius. No statistical significance or fixed dwell period is required.

## Closure

Close the rollback when smoke tests pass and error rate and p95 latency are back within the pre-release baseline for 15 minutes.

arguments.content:
# Private Deployment Rollback — Evidence-Gated Policy

Owner: SRE On-call and Private Deployments  
Status: reviewed candidate  
Scope: Redwood-managed private VPC and on-prem deployments.

## Contract

Rollback is a controlled incident operation. Restore service rapidly, but do not mutate deployment state until the minimum evidence, authority, and recoverability gates below are satisfied. The sole exception is imminent customer harm: the Incident Commander (IC) may authorize immediate traffic isolation while evidence capture continues.

## 1. Declare and contain

1. Open or link the incident; record deployment, tenant/cohort, current and last-known-good signed versions, start time, suspected failure mode, operator, and IC.
2. Pause the rollout. For imminent harm, isolate the new cohort by routing old:100/new:0. Traffic isolation is containment, not approval to restore state.
3. Assign Field Operator (execution), SRE On-call/IC (rollback authority), Release Owner (version and stage ownership), and Security/Evidence Custodian for provenance, exposure, regulated environments, or suspected corruption. Notify the customer liaison when contract or customer impact requires it.

## 2. Minimum evidence gate

Before artifact, operator, network, or persistent-state mutation, attach or durably reference:

- 30 minutes of pre-change baseline and the complete rollout window for error rate, p50/p95 latency, request rate, token/request, KV-cache health, GPU saturation, and quality smoke results;
- signed manifest, checksum/SBOM verification, current/target versions, operator logs, and rollout status;
- snapshot/checkpoint identifier, creation time, off-host location, checksum/restore token, and schema/version compatibility result;
- for network-affecting changes: Terraform plan/diff, peering and route state, DNS stamp/delegation/propagation evidence, endpoint reachability, and a last-known-good network checkpoint;
- an action timeline with actor and timestamp.

If capture is impossible, the IC records the missing item, why delay is unsafe, and a named owner and deadline. Suspected corruption requires selecting a snapshot before the suspected window; never overwrite the only evidence-bearing snapshot.

## 3. Decision and approvals

Immediate rollback is mandatory for data corruption or PII exposure, signature/SBOM failure, model compatibility failure, customer SLA breach, p95 latency >50% above baseline or >500 ms for 10 minutes, error rate >0.5 percentage points with significant 30-minute evidence, KV-cache hit-rate drop >15 points with >10% backend-load increase, or GPU utilization >95% for 5 minutes.

- IC/SRE authorizes emergency rollback.
- Release Owner confirms the last-known-good signed version unless unavailable during active harm; the IC records that exception.
- Security/Evidence Custodian approval is required before state restore for suspected corruption/exposure and before using artifacts with unresolved provenance.
- Customer-operator approval is required when the deployment contract assigns the customer control of production changes or the action crosses an agreed traffic/change boundary.
- No one may bypass a non-reversible schema/downgrade gate. Prefer traffic rollback without state restore until compatibility is proven.

## 4. Execute in order

1. Quiesce new-version traffic and freeze further automation.
2. Execute `redwoodctl rollout rollback --target <deployment-id> --to-version <previous-semver> --preserve-snapshots`.
3. If automation fails, install only the verified signed archive and revert the operator manifest.
4. Restore state only if required and approved: lock concurrent state changes, verify snapshot checksum/restore token and version/schema compatibility, restore to the isolated target, run invariant validation, then reopen traffic.
5. For network rollback, revert only from the reviewed plan/checkpoint; verify routes/peering, DNS stamp propagation/delegation, endpoint reachability, and resolver behavior before reopening traffic.

## 5. Validate and close

Keep traffic on the last-known-good version until smoke tests, persistent-request/KV invariants, network checks when applicable, and all gating metrics are within the pre-release baseline for 60 continuous minutes. Preserve the rollback evidence package and timeline. Retain it at least 90 days for regulated customers or longer when the customer telemetry/evidence contract requires. Deliver the incident brief and owned remediation plan within 72 hours; complete any required postmortem on the governing incident schedule.

## Stop conditions

Stop and escalate rather than improvise when the prior artifact is unsigned/unavailable, snapshot identity or compatibility is unverified, evidence indicates corruption outside the chosen recovery point, network state differs from the reviewed plan, required customer authority is absent, or post-restore invariants fail.

              "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Private Deployment Rollback — Evidence-Gated Policy\nSource: Aisha Bello / Redwood Inference\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/private-deployment-rollback.md\nWorkspace: task/aisha-private-rollback-evidence\n\n# Private Deployment Rollback — Evidence-Gated Policy\n\nOwner: SRE On-call and Private Deployments  \nStatus: reviewed candidate  \nScope: Redwood-managed private VPC and on-prem deployments.\n\n## Contract\n\nRollback is a controlled incident operation. Restore service rapidly, but do not mutate deployment state until the minimum evidence, authority, and recoverability gates below are satisfied. The sole exception is imminent customer harm: the Incident Commander (IC) may authorize immediate traffic isolation while evidence capture continues.\n\n## 1. Declare and contain\n\n1. Open or link the incident; record deployment, tenant/cohort, current and last-known-good signed versions, start time, suspected failure mode, operator, and IC.\n2. Pause the rollout. For imminent harm, isolate the new cohort by routing old:100/new:0. Traffic isolation is containment, not approval to restore state.\n3. Assign Field Operator (execution), SRE On-call/IC (rollback authority), Release Owner (version and stage ownership), and Security/Evidence Custodian for provenance, exposure, regulated environments, or suspected corruption. Notify the customer liaison when contract or customer impact requires it.\n\n## 2. Minimum evidence gate\n\nBefore artifact, operator, network, or persistent-state mutation, attach or durably reference:\n\n- 30 minutes of pre-change baseline and the complete rollout window for error rate, p50/p95 latency, request rate, token/request, KV-cache health, GPU saturation, and quality smoke results;\n- signed manifest, checksum/SBOM verification, current/target versions, operator logs, and rollout status;\n- snapshot/checkpoint identifier, creation time, off-host location, checksum/restore token, and schema/version compatibility result;\n- for network-affecting changes: Terraform plan/diff, peering and route state, DNS stamp/delegation/propagation evidence, endpoint reachability, and a last-known-good network checkpoint;\n- an action timeline with actor and timestamp.\n\nIf capture is impossible, the IC records the missing item, why delay is unsafe, and a named owner and deadline. Suspected corruption requires selecting a snapshot before the suspected window; never overwrite the only evidence-bearing snapshot.\n\n## 3. Decision and approvals",

            "content": "# Private Deployment Rollback — Evidence-Gated Policy\n\nOwner: SRE On-call and Private Deployments  \nStatus: reviewed candidate  \nScope: Redwood-managed private VPC and on-prem deployments.\n\n## Contract\n\nRollback is a controlled incident operation. Open or link the incident; record deployment, tenant/cohort, current and last-known-good signed versions, start time, suspected failure mode, operator, and IC.\n2. Pause the rollout. For imminent harm, isolate the new cohort by routing old:100/new:0. Traffic isolation is containment, not approval to restore state.\n3. Assign Field Operator (execution), SRE On-call/IC (rollback authority), Release Owner (version and stage ownership), and Security/Evidence Custodian for provenance, exposure, regulated environments, or suspected corruption. Notify the customer liaison when contract or customer impact requires it.\n\n## 2. Minimum evidence gate\n\nBefore artifact, operator, network, or persistent-state mutation, attach or durably reference:\n\n- 30 minutes of pre-change baseline and the complete rollout window for error rate, p50/p95 latency, request rate, token/request, KV-cache health, GPU saturation, and quality smoke results;\n- signed manifest, checksum/SBOM verification, current/target versions, operator logs, and rollout status;\n- snapshot/checkpoint identifier, creation time, off-host location, checksum/restore token, and schema/version compatibility result;\n- for network-affecting changes: Terraform plan/diff, peering and route state, DNS stamp/delegation/propagation evidence, endpoint reachability, and a last-known-good network checkpoint;\n- an action timeline with actor and timestamp.\n\nIf capture is impossible, the IC records the missing item, why delay is unsafe, and a named owner and deadline. Suspected corruption requires selecting a snapshot before the suspected window; never overwrite the only evidence-bearing snapshot.\n\n## 3. # Private Deployment Rollback — Evidence-Gated Policy

Owner: SRE On-call and Private Deployments  
Status: reviewed candidate  
Scope: Redwood-managed private VPC and on-prem deployments.

## Contract

Rollback is a controlled incident operation. Restore service rapidly, but do not mutate deployment state until the minimum evidence, authority, and recoverability gates below are satisfied. The sole exception is imminent customer harm: the Incident Commander (IC) may authorize immediate traffic isolation while evidence capture continues.

## 1. Declare and contain

1. Open or link the incident; record deployment, tenant/cohort, current and last-known-good signed versions, start time, suspected failure mode, operator, and IC.
2. Pause the rollout. For imminent harm, isolate the new cohort by routing old:100/new:0. Traffic isolation is containment, not approval to restore state.
3. Assign Field Operator (execution), SRE On-call/IC (rollback authority), Release Owner (version and stage ownership), and Security/Evidence Custodian for provenance, exposure, regulated environments, or suspected corruption. Notify the customer liaison when contract or customer impact requires it.

## 2. Minimum evidence gate

Before artifact, operator, network, or persistent-state mutation, attach or durably reference:

- 30 minutes of pre-change baseline and the complete rollout window for error rate, p50/p95 latency, request rate, token/request, KV-cache health, GPU saturation, and quality smoke results;
- signed manifest, checksum/SBOM verification, current/target versions, operator logs, and rollout status;
- snapshot/checkpoint identifier, creation time, off-host location, checksum/restore token, and schema/version compatibility result;
- for network-affecting changes: Terraform plan/diff, peering and route state, DNS stamp/delegation/propagation evidence, endpoint reachability, and a last-known-good network checkpoint;
- an action timeline with actor and timestamp.

If capture is impossible, the IC records the missing item, why delay is unsafe, and a named owner and deadline. Suspected corruption requires selecting a snapshot before the suspected window; never overwrite the only evidence-bearing snapshot.

## 3. Decision and approvals

- an action timeline with actor and timestamp.

If capture is impossible, the IC records the missing item, why delay is unsafe, and a named owner and deadline. Suspected corruption requires selecting a snapshot before the suspected window; never overwrite the only evidence-bearing snapshot.

## 3. Decision and approvals

Immediate rollback is mandatory for data corruption or PII exposure, signature/SBOM failure, model compatibility failure, customer SLA breach, p95 latency >50% above baseline or >500 ms for 10 minutes, error rate >0.5 percentage points with significant 30-minute evidence, KV-cache hit-rate drop >15 points with >10% backend-load increase, or GPU utilization >95% for 5 minutes.

- IC/SRE authorizes emergency rollback.
- Release Owner confirms the last-known-good signed version unless unavailable during active harm; the IC records that exception.
- Security/Evidence Custodian approval is required before state restore for suspected corruption/exposure and before using artifacts with unresolved provenance.
- Customer-operator approval is required when the deployment contract assigns the customer control of production changes or the action crosses an agreed traffic/change boundary.
- No one may bypass a non-reversible schema/downgrade gate. Prefer traffic rollback without state restore until compatibility is proven.

## 4. Execute in order

1. Quiesce new-version traffic and freeze further automation.
2. Execute `redwoodctl rollout rollback --target <deployment-id> --to-version <previous-semver> --preserve-snapshots`.
3. If automation fails, install only the verified signed archive and revert the operator manifest.
4. Restore state only if required and approved: lock concurrent state changes, verify snapshot checksum/restore token and version/schema compatibility, restore to the isolated target, run invariant validation, then reopen traffic.
5. For network rollback, revert only from the reviewed plan/checkpoint; verify routes/peering, DNS stamp propagation/delegation, endpoint reachability, and resolver behavior before reopening traffic.

## 5. Validate and close

5. For network rollback, revert only from the reviewed plan/checkpoint; verify routes/peering, DNS stamp propagation/delegation, endpoint reachability, and resolver behavior before reopening traffic.

## 5. Validate and close

Keep traffic on the last-known-good version until smoke tests, persistent-request/KV invariants, network checks when applicable, and all gating metrics are within the pre-release baseline for 60 continuous minutes. Preserve the rollback evidence package and timeline. Retain it at least 90 days for regulated customers or longer when the customer telemetry/evidence contract requires. Deliver the incident brief and owned remediation plan within 72 hours; complete any required postmortem on the governing incident schedule.

## Stop conditions

Stop and escalate rather than improvise when the prior artifact is unsigned/unavailable, snapshot identity or compatibility is unverified, evidence indicates corruption outside the chosen recovery point, network state differs from the reviewed plan, required customer authority is absent, or post-restore invariants fail.

The sole exception is imminent customer harm: the Incident Commander (IC) may authorize immediate traffic isolation while evidence capture continues.\n\n## 1. Declare and contain\n\n1. Open or link the incident; record deployment, tenant/cohort, current and last-known-good signed versions, start time, suspected failure mode, operator, and IC.\n2. Pause the rollout. For imminent harm, isolate the new cohort by routing old:100/new:0. Traffic isolation is containment, not approval to restore state.\n3. Assign Field Operator (execution), SRE On-call/IC (rollback authority), Release Owner (version and stage ownership), and Security/Evidence Custodian for provenance, exposure, regulated environments, or suspected corruption. Notify the customer liaison when contract or customer impact requires it.\n\n## 2. Minimum evidence gate\n\nBefore artifact, operator, network, or persistent-state mutation, attach or durably reference:\n\n- 30 minutes of pre-change baseline and the complete rollout window for error rate, p50/p95 latency, request rate, token/request, KV-cache health, GPU saturation, and quality smoke results;\n- signed manifest, checksum/SBOM verification, current/target versions, operator logs, and rollout status;\n- snapshot/checkpoint identifier, creation time, off-host location, checksum/restore token, and schema/version compatibility result;\n- for network-affecting changes: Terraform plan/diff, peering and route state, DNS stamp/delegation/propagation evidence, endpoint reachability, and a last-known-good network checkpoint;\n- an action timeline with actor and timestamp.\n\nIf capture is impossible, the IC records the missing item, why delay is unsafe, and a named owner and deadline. Suspected corruption requires selecting a snapshot before the suspected window; never overwrite the only evidence-bearing snapshot.\n\n## 3. Decision and approvals",

      "text": "[Document context]\nTitle: Private Deployment Rollback — Evidence-Gated Policy\nSource: Aisha Bello / Redwood Inference\nPath: /knowledge/runbooks/private-deployment-rollback.md\nWorkspace: task/aisha-private-rollback-evidence\n\ncheckpoint;\n- an action timeline with actor and timestamp.\n\nIf capture is impossible, the IC records the missing item, why delay is unsafe, and a named owner and deadline. Suspected corruption requires selecting a snapshot before the suspected window; never overwrite the only evidence-bearing snapshot.\n\n## 3. Decision and approvals\n\nImmediate rollback is mandatory for data corruption or PII exposure, signature/SBOM failure, model compatibility failure, customer SLA breach, p95 latency >50% above baseline or >500 ms for 10 minutes, error rate >0.5 percentage points with significant 30-minute evidence, KV-cache hit-rate drop >15 points with >10% backend-load increase, or GPU utilization >95% for 5 minutes.\n\n- IC/SRE authorizes emergency rollback.\n- Release Owner confirms the last-known-good signed version unless unavailable during active harm; the IC records that exception.\n- Security/Evidence Custodian approval is required before state restore for suspected corruption/exposure and before using artifacts with unresolved provenance.\n- Customer-operator approval is required when the deployment contract assigns the customer control of production changes or the action crosses an agreed traffic/change boundary.\n- No one may bypass a non-reversible schema/downgrade gate. Prefer traffic rollback without state restore until compatibility is proven.\n\n## 4. Execute in order\n\n1. Quiesce new-version traffic and freeze further automation.\n2. Execute `redwoodctl rollout rollback --target <deployment-id> --to-version <previous-semver> --preserve-snapshots`.\n3. If automation fails, install only the verified signed archive and revert the operator manifest.\n4. Restore state only if required and approved: lock concurrent state changes, verify snapshot checksum/restore token and version/schema compatibility, restore to the isolated target, run invariant validation, then reopen traffic.\n5. For network rollback, revert only from the reviewed plan/checkpoint; verify routes/peering, DNS stamp propagation/delegation, endpoint reachability, and resolver behavior before reopening traffic.\n\n## 5. Validate and close",

document.title: Private Deployment Rollback — Evidence-Gated Policy
document.content:
# Private Deployment Rollback — Evidence-Gated Policy

Owner: SRE On-call and Private Deployments  
Status: reviewed candidate  
Scope: Redwood-managed private VPC and on-prem deployments.

## Contract

Rollback is a controlled incident operation. Restore service rapidly, but do not mutate deployment state until the minimum evidence, authority, and recoverability gates below are satisfied. The sole exception is imminent customer harm: the Incident Commander (IC) may authorize immediate traffic isolation while evidence capture continues.

## 1. Declare and contain

1. Open or link the incident; record deployment, tenant/cohort, current and last-known-good signed versions, start time, suspected failure mode, operator, and IC.
2. Pause the rollout. For imminent harm, isolate the new cohort by routing old:100/new:0. Traffic isolation is containment, not approval to restore state.
3. Assign Field Operator (execution), SRE On-call/IC (rollback authority), Release Owner (version and stage ownership), and Security/Evidence Custodian for provenance, exposure, regulated environments, or suspected corruption. Notify the customer liaison when contract or customer impact requires it.

## 2. Minimum evidence gate

Before artifact, operator, network, or persistent-state mutation, attach or durably reference:

- 30 minutes of pre-change baseline and the complete rollout window for error rate, p50/p95 latency, request rate, token/request, KV-cache health, GPU saturation, and quality smoke results;
- signed manifest, checksum/SBOM verification, current/target versions, operator logs, and rollout status;
- snapshot/checkpoint identifier, creation time, off-host location, checksum/restore token, and schema/version compatibility result;
- for network-affecting changes: Terraform plan/diff, peering and route state, DNS stamp/delegation/propagation evidence, endpoint reachability, and a last-known-good network checkpoint;
- an action timeline with actor and timestamp.

If capture is impossible, the IC records the missing item, why delay is unsafe, and a named owner and deadline. Suspected corruption requires selecting a snapshot before the suspected window; never overwrite the only evidence-bearing snapshot.

## 3. Decision and approvals

Immediate rollback is mandatory for data corruption or PII exposure, signature/SBOM failure, model compatibility failure, customer SLA breach, p95 latency >50% above baseline or >500 ms for 10 minutes, error rate >0.5 percentage points with significant 30-minute evidence, KV-cache hit-rate drop >15 points with >10% backend-load increase, or GPU utilization >95% for 5 minutes.

- IC/SRE authorizes emergency rollback.
- Release Owner confirms the last-known-good signed version unless unavailable during active harm; the IC records that exception.
- Security/Evidence Custodian approval is required before state restore for suspected corruption/exposure and before using artifacts with unresolved provenance.
- Customer-operator approval is required when the deployment contract assigns the customer control of production changes or the action crosses an agreed traffic/change boundary.
- No one may bypass a non-reversible schema/downgrade gate. Prefer traffic rollback without state restore until compatibility is proven.

## 4. Execute in order

1. Quiesce new-version traffic and freeze further automation.
2. Execute `redwoodctl rollout rollback --target <deployment-id> --to-version <previous-semver> --preserve-snapshots`.
3. If automation fails, install only the verified signed archive and revert the operator manifest.
4. Restore state only if required and approved: lock concurrent state changes, verify snapshot checksum/restore token and version/schema compatibility, restore to the isolated target, run invariant validation, then reopen traffic.
5. For network rollback, revert only from the reviewed plan/checkpoint; verify routes/peering, DNS stamp propagation/delegation, endpoint reachability, and resolver behavior before reopening traffic.

## 5. Validate and close

Keep traffic on the last-known-good version until smoke tests, persistent-request/KV invariants, network checks when applicable, and all gating metrics are within the pre-release baseline for 60 continuous minutes. Preserve the rollback evidence package and timeline. Retain it at least 90 days for regulated customers or longer when the customer telemetry/evidence contract requires. Deliver the incident brief and owned remediation plan within 72 hours; complete any required postmortem on the governing incident schedule.

## Stop conditions

Stop and escalate rather than improvise when the prior artifact is unsigned/unavailable, snapshot identity or compatibility is unverified, evidence indicates corruption outside the chosen recovery point, network state differs from the reviewed plan, required customer authority is absent, or post-restore invariants fail.

Verification shows the personal branch has the evidence-gated runbook and reviewed semantic memory with matching hashes, while the experiment artifact is absent. I’m removing both temporary branches now.

Published exactly one policy: the evidence-gated candidate.

## Candidates

1. Fast recovery — rejected

- Field operator immediately routes 100% to the last-known-good version.
- No prerequisite evidence or approval gate during active impact.
- Uses the latest available snapshot if needed.
- Validates latency, errors, and smoke tests for 15 minutes.
- Collects evidence and approvals after restoration.

Primary weakness: it assumes universal operator authority, snapshot compatibility, and sufficient network state. Those assumptions conflict with approval, evidence-preservation, and restore-safety guidance.

2. Evidence-gated — accepted

- Immediately pauses rollout and permits IC-authorized traffic isolation for imminent harm.
- Requires a pre-mutation evidence package covering telemetry, provenance, snapshots, schema compatibility, and—when applicable—network plans, routes, peering, DNS, and reachability.
- Requires IC/SRE authorization plus applicable Release Owner, Security/Evidence Custodian, and customer-operator approvals.
- Prohibits bypassing non-reversible downgrade gates.
- Restores state only after snapshot identity, checksum, schema compatibility, and invariants are verified.
- Requires 60 continuous minutes at baseline before closure.
- Defines explicit stop-and-escalate conditions.

This is the selected policy as written, not a hybrid with the fast candidate.

## Evidence

The decision was principally supported by:

- `dsid_75393a098ca44803ae097c4b2d543199` — published staged-rollout contract: signed artifacts, pre-release snapshots, deterministic rollback gates, evidence retention, and 60-minute validation.
- `dsid_a6e7e19f598943b692d84638aa9a9a6d` — compliance-anchored rollback: IC, evidence custodian, deployment lead, and evidence-preservation requirements.
- `dsid_b928a31ac74644d2b70298634002bdff` — staged network rollout: DNS propagation, peering guardrails, preflight checks, and reversible checkpoints.
- `dsid_67fd0fa35c704bcbac0e7aa23fcd6285` — snapshot guidance: incident approval, recovery-point selection, state locking, and air-gapped recovery considerations. This source was marked in review, so it was corroborative rather than the sole policy basis.
- `dsid_499ce734c806422e980396966f03515b` — incident/cutover guidance: evidence before mutation, SRE approval for policy changes, checkpoint preservation, and post-rollback validation.
